steps.title: Receive cognizable information in any mode
steps.text: Receive every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence irrespective of the area in which the offence was committed; it may be given to the Station House Officer (SHO) orally, in writing, or through electronic communication [Section 173(1) BNSS].
legal_basis: Section 173(1) BNSS 2023
steps.triage_why: General statutory definition of receiving information; the FIR is already registered in this case.

ticks.do: Receive every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence irrespective of the area in which the offence was committed [Section 173(1) BNSS].
Accept information given to the Station House Officer (SHO) in any of the modes below.
sub: Orally
In writing
Through electronic communication

details.text: There is no hard and fast rule that the informant must be the aggrieved person or victim; information may be given by any person.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: It is not necessary that first information be given only by a person with entire knowledge of the facts; it may be merely hearsay [Shew Pru v. King, AIR 1941 Rang 209].
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: The practice of insisting on written information about a cognizable offence before registering a case is not correct and should be dispensed with.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

steps.title: Register every cognizable complaint compulsorily
steps.text: The complaint of a cognizable offence shall compulsorily be registered; registration of the FIR is mandatory even if the offence occurred outside the territorial jurisdiction of the police station, and refusal on the jurisdiction ground is prohibited.
legal_basis: Section 173(1) BNSS 2023
Section 199(c) BNS 2023 (officer's penal liability for default)
steps.triage_why: General rule on mandatory registration and jurisdiction; not a step for the IO once the case is registered.

ticks.do: Register the complaint of a cognizable offence compulsorily.
Register the FIR even if the offence occurred outside the territorial jurisdiction of the police station.
Do not refuse registration on the ground of jurisdiction.

details.text: A police officer who defaults in registering an offence under BNS Sections 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 70, 71, 74, 76, 77, 79, 124, 143, 144 is himself liable for a punishable offence under Section 199(c) BNS.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: The Section 199(c) BNS punishment for an officer who fails to record information under Section 173(1) BNSS in relation to those offences is rigorous imprisonment for not less than six months, extendable to two years, and fine.
details.citation: BPR&D - Final SOP on Preliminary Enquiry, 2023 (Section 173(3) BNSS)

details.text: The officer has no power to refuse to enter received information about a cognizable offence in the FIR; refusal is possible only if the information is vague and not adequate enough to enable commencement of an investigation.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: The FIR is not an encyclopedia: it is enough if the officer, on the information given, suspects the commission of a cognizable offence — he need not be convinced or satisfied that one has been committed.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Do not defer registration on the plea of verifying the truth of the information, and do not withhold recording of the FIR for the collection of further details.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Refusal to record an FIR because the place of crime is outside territorial jurisdiction amounts to dereliction of duty; the officer must record the case and forward it (AIR 1993 SC 2644).
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: A police officer cannot refuse to record the FIR on the ground of having no territorial jurisdiction over the place of offence.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Refusal to record the FIR for the specified sexual/acid-attack offences is punishable under Section 166A IPC [now BNS 199].
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: The informant/victim/aggrieved party has no right to withdraw the case once the FIR is registered.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

steps.title: Verify the offence is cognizable before registering
steps.text: Before registering, verify whether the offence disclosed is cognizable or non-cognizable: an FIR (including a Zero FIR) can be registered only for a cognizable offence.
legal_basis: Section 173(1) BNSS 2023
Section 174 BNSS 2023
steps.triage_why: Pre-registration verification step; the case is already registered.

ticks.do: Verify before registering whether the offence disclosed is cognizable or non-cognizable.
notes: An FIR, including a Zero FIR, can be registered only for a cognizable offence.

details.text: The essential condition for recording an FIR is information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence; if the information discloses more offences than one, at least one must be cognizable for direct registration by the officer in charge.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Take care that the informant is not exaggerating the occurrence or giving the colour of a cognizable offence to a non-cognizable incident; informants tend to give coloured statements out of excitement or prejudice.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

steps.title: Reduce oral information to writing and sign it
steps.text: If the information is given orally, reduce it to writing (by the SHO or under his supervision), read it over to the informant, and obtain the informant's signature on every such written complaint; enter its substance in the prescribed station book [Section 173(1)(i) BNSS].
legal_basis: Section 173(1)(i) BNSS 2023
steps.triage_why: Statutory requirement under Section 173(1)(i) BNSS to ensure the integrity of the first account and informant's consent.

ticks.do: Reduce the information to writing where it is given orally, by the SHO or under his supervision [Section 173(1)(i) BNSS].
Read the written information over to the informant.
Obtain the informant's signature on every such written complaint.
Enter the substance of the information in the prescribed station book.

details.text: Record in plain and simple words, in the language of the victim as far as possible.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: The idea behind reading over the recorded information and obtaining the informant's signature is to ensure that what has been reduced to writing is a true and faithful version of the information given.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: If the informant cannot sign, take his right/left hand thumb impression; if he cannot speak the regional language, seek the service of an interpreter; read the recorded statement over to an illiterate informant 2-3 times.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: If after recording the information the informant refuses to sign the report, he may be prosecuted for the offence under Section 180 IPC.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Absence of the informant's signature on the FIR does not vitiate or nullify it; the FIR is still admissible in evidence.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: The officer in charge, even if outside the police station building, can record the first information, forward it for registering an FIR at the police station, and commence and continue the investigation.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: If the officer in charge who registered the case is not the SHO, he shall forthwith inform the SHO to exercise the discretionary powers.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: At a Police Out-Post the officer in charge cannot prepare an FIR (he is not a Station House Officer): he enters the facts in the Out-Post general diary and sends the report or the informant as expeditiously as possible to the police station; in an emergency he proceeds to the scene, takes steps to arrest the accused and recover stolen property pending the SHO's arrival, and sees to the proper guarding of the scene.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

steps.title: Capture every required particular in the FIR
steps.text: Record the FIR as a truthful, complete first account — neither minimized nor exaggerated: note the time of occurrence (occurrence and reporting times must be logical), motive, preparation and previous/subsequent conduct of the accused if known, the modus operandi, identity or physical features of the accused with the circumstances of identification (light, distance, line of visibility), names of eyewitnesses, injuries seen on the informant or witnesses, and the correct value and identifying marks of property involved.
steps.triage_why: Best practice for a high-quality investigation, but the legal validity of the FIR doesn't depend on the inclusion of every detail listed.

ticks.do: Record the FIR as a truthful, complete first account, neither minimized nor exaggerated.
Note each of the following particulars in the FIR.
sub: The time of occurrence (occurrence and reporting times must be logical)
The motive, preparation and previous or subsequent conduct of the accused if known
The modus operandi
The identity or physical features of the accused with the circumstances of identification (light, distance, line of visibility)
The names of eyewitnesses
The injuries seen on the informant or witnesses
The correct value and identifying marks of property involved

details.text: Cover the eleven 'W's for a comprehensive FIR: what information, informant's capacity (eyewitness/victim/hearsay), who committed, who is the victim, when, where, why (motive), which way it happened (role of each accused, weapon), who else was present, what was taken away, what traces were left.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Enter serially the names of known/suspected/unknown accused with full particulars; record eyewitness names and the names of persons to whom the complainant reported the accused's names immediately after the occurrence — if available first-hand information is not noted, the defence may term it fabrication and afterthought.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: The informant should distinguish between what he saw, knew and heard; where a particular person is suspected, clearly specify the facts on which the suspicion is based.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Explain any delay in lodging the FIR believably in the FIR itself (8th column); unexplained delay creates suspicion of afterthought, though delay in filing an FIR in a rape case cannot be used against the prosecution.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Do not interpolate anything after the FIR has been written; avoid scoring out what has been written — in unavoidable cases draw a line across the words keeping them legible and the recording officer should initial it.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Do not avoid the crucial facts of the First Information Statement while filling the 12th column of the FIR, and do not include in column 12 information that was not stated in the first information.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Mention correctly the value of property stolen, damaged or lost — do not lessen it to improve statistics — and clearly note special identifying marks with a detailed description.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: If the incident happened after sunset, explain the source of light; record the direction and distance of the place of occurrence from the police station in the last part of the statement; record the informant's contact number and e-mail ID; if the victim does not come to give the statement, explain the reason for his absence.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: If the informant knows the names of the occurrence/ocular witnesses, record them in the First Information Statement.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

steps.title: Protect the informant's dignity while recording
steps.text: Treat the informant properly while taking the FIR: allow nobody to prompt statements, do not distort or exaggerate the information given, never jump to conclusions, do not make the informant wait long, do not insult, abuse or ridicule him, do not deprive him of the public utilities at the police station for his primary needs, put a stressed informant at ease, brief him about his rights and the services rendered by the police, and if an injured person comes to the station, do not record the statement there — direct him to hospital immediately and record the statement at the hospital.
steps.triage_why: Professional conduct and victim care; while important, omission is not a statutory failure that defeats prosecution.

ticks.do: Treat the informant properly while taking the FIR, observing each point below.
sub: Allow nobody to prompt statements
Do not distort or exaggerate the information given
Never jump to conclusions
Do not make the informant wait long
Do not insult, abuse or ridicule him
Do not deprive him of the public utilities at the police station for his primary needs
Put a stressed informant at ease
Brief him about his rights and the services rendered by the police

ticks.do: Direct an injured person who comes to the station to hospital immediately instead of recording his statement there.
Record that injured person's statement at the hospital.

details.text: Be humble, polite and simple, using very polite language with senior citizens; if a written complaint has omissions, clarify the relevant details and then record the information; put the stressed informant at ease before recording.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: While taking the statement of an injured person, note the position of the injury.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

steps.title: Get victim's statement recorded before a Magistrate
steps.text: At the earliest possible opportunity, take steps to have the statement of such a victim recorded before a Magistrate under Section 183(6)(a) BNSS.
legal_basis: Section 173(1)(c) BNSS 2023
Section 183(6)(a) BNSS 2023
steps.deadline: At the earliest possible opportunity / as promptly as possible [Section 173(1)(c) BNSS read with Section 183(6)(a) BNSS]
steps.applies_when: Victim of a BNS 64-71, 74-79 or 124 offence (in particular disabled victims whose information was recorded under Section 173(1)(ii) BNSS)
steps.triage_why: Statutory duty under Section 183(6)(a) BNSS for victims of sexual offences; failure to record this promptly can weaken the case or be seen as a procedural lapse.

ticks.do: Take steps at the earliest possible opportunity to have the statement of such a victim recorded before a Magistrate under Section 183(6)(a) BNSS [Section 173(1)(c) BNSS].
notes: Duty of the investigating police officer.

details.text: If possible have the statement recorded by a woman Magistrate; in her absence, before a male Magistrate keeping a woman present, following the SOP on recording of statements and confessional statements.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

steps.title: Record woman victim's sexual-offence information by woman officer
steps.text: If information of an offence under BNS Sections 64 to 71, 74 to 79, or 124 is given by the woman victim, that information shall be recorded by a woman police officer, and in her absence by any woman officer [proviso to Section 173(1) BNSS].
legal_basis: Proviso to Section 173(1) BNSS 2023
steps.applies_when: Information of a BNS 64-71, 74-79 or 124 offence given by the woman victim
steps.triage_why: Statutory mandate under the proviso to Section 173(1) BNSS for offences under BNS 64 (rape); failure to use a woman officer is a legal violation.

ticks.do: Record information of an offence under BNS Sections 64 to 71, 74 to 79, or 124 given by the woman victim
sub: recorded through a woman police officer
in her absence, recorded by any woman officer [proviso to Section 173(1) BNSS]

details.text: For these offences strictly comply with Section 173(1)(a), (b) and (c) BNSS as a package: recording at the residence of the person wishing to give the information or a place of that person's choice with an interpreter/special educator as the occasion may be, videography of the recording, and action as promptly as possible to record the statement before the Magistrate under Section 183(6)(a) BNSS.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: In sexual offence cases record the statement in the language of the victim as far as possible, use simple and humble language, do not embarrass the victim, and do not insult an accompanying NGO person; woman police officers may be designated as Victim Liaison Officers to assist, counsel and support the victim.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

steps.title: Obtain the informant's signature within three days
steps.text: For information given through electronic communication, contact the informant (by mobile phone, e-mail or personal contact), have him attend the police station and sign the information within three days of its receipt, and register it as an FIR only if the signature is made within that period [Section 173(1)(ii) BNSS].
legal_basis: Section 173(1)(ii) BNSS 2023
steps.deadline: Signature of the informant within 3 days of receipt of the electronic information [Section 173(1)(ii) BNSS]
steps.triage_why: Applies only if information was given via electronic communication; the case summary does not specify the mode of reporting.

ticks.do: Contact the informant who gave information through electronic communication, by any of the means below [Section 173(1)(ii) BNSS].
sub: Mobile phone
E-mail
Personal contact

ticks.do: Have the informant attend the police station and sign the information within three days of its receipt.
Register the information as an FIR only if the signature is made within that period.

details.text: After obtaining the signature of the informant, the SHO has two options: register the FIR under Section 173(1) BNSS, or take action for a preliminary inquiry under Section 173(3) BNSS.

details.text: If the informant/complainant does not remain present to sign within the three-day time limit given in the law, the SHO must make a note to that effect in the Station Diary.

conflicts.description: kerala_police_sop_2020 p.19 (CrPC-era) states that telegram/telephone/WhatsApp/other digital information cannot be taken directly for registering an FIR for want of the informant's signature — the officer must first contact the sender and collect the information (or, per p.20, register suo motu); Section 173(1)(ii) BNSS and guj_cid_29_sops_2024 SOP 8 p.32 now expressly permit electronic information to be received and registered once the informant signs within three days.
conflicts.resolution: Law prevails: the BNSS 2023 electronic-information procedure with the 3-day signature window is canonical; the Kerala position reflects the superseded CrPC regime.

steps.title: Act immediately on serious electronic information
steps.text: If electronically received information states that a serious and heinous offence has been committed or that there is a likelihood of such an offence, or mentions an incident by which the law and order situation may deteriorate, the SHO must take immediate action to verify the truth of the information without waiting for the complainant to come to the police station.
steps.deadline: Immediately, without waiting for the complainant to come to the police station (SOP 8 guideline (vii))
steps.triage_why: Applies to the verification phase of electronic information before/during FIR registration.

ticks.do: Take immediate action, as SHO, to verify the truth of electronically received information falling in any of the categories below, without waiting for the complainant to come to the police station.
sub: Information that a serious and heinous offence has been committed
Information that there is a likelihood of such an offence
Information mentioning an incident by which the law and order situation may deteriorate

details.text: If the information indicates a serious offence or danger to a person's life and the informant, being very old or infirm, is unable to come to the police station to sign, the SHO must depute an officer immediately to obtain the signature on the report of the informant/victim.

steps.title: Log electronic information in the e-FIR Register
steps.text: Receive information about an offence through the police station's official mobile number, e-mail ID or citizen portal; enter electronic information relating to a cognizable offence in a separate 'e-FIR Register' (Appendix-A format) maintained in every police station — downloading and keeping the information on the station computer if possible — and enter its particulars in the Station Diary.
steps.triage_why: Administrative record-keeping for e-FIRs; not a core investigative step for the IO.

ticks.do: Receive information about an offence through any of the police station's channels.
sub: The official mobile number
The e-mail ID
The citizen portal

ticks.do: Enter electronic information relating to a cognizable offence in the separate 'e-FIR Register' (Appendix-A format) maintained in every police station.
Download the information and keep it on the station computer where possible.
Enter the particulars of the information in the Station Diary.

details.text: Appendix-A columns include: serial number, date/time and mode of receipt, informant's name/address/mobile/e-mail, proof of residence and identity (Aadhaar/PAN/passport, Yes/No), brief particulars of the offence with Station Diary entry number, cognizable/non-cognizable type, date/time and manner in which the informant was told to attend for signature, steps taken by the SHO after signature (preliminary inquiry or FIR registration number with cross reference), and the Station Diary entry of the action taken or of the informant's failure to sign within the time limit.

steps.title: Publish and display police station contact channels
steps.text: The district Superintendent of Police must publish the official/registered WhatsApp-enabled mobile number and Government e-mail address of every police station under his jurisdiction, and the SHO must display them outside the police station in such a manner that the public can see them easily.
steps.responsible: Superintendent of Police; Station House Officer
steps.triage_why: Administrative duty of the SP and SHO regarding public notices, not an investigative step.

conflicts.resolution: Law prevails: the BNSS 2023 formulation (informant or victim) is canonical; the narrower CrPC recipient is superseded.

steps.text: Forthwith send the FIR report to the Magistrate empowered to take cognizance of the offence [Section 176 BNSS].
legal_basis: Section 176 BNSS 2023
Section 210 BNSS 2023 (cognizance; police report valid in electronic mode)
steps.deadline: Forthwith [Section 176 BNSS; Section 157 CrPC as printed in older sources]
steps.triage_why: Statutory duty under Section 176 BNSS; failure to notify the Magistrate can lead to the investigation being questioned.

details.text: Send the original FIR to the court empowered for the special law concerned: UAPA cases to the District Sessions Court, POCSO Act cases to the specially designated Sessions Court, NDPS and SC/ST (PoA) Act cases to their Special Courts where constituted, and Prevention of Corruption Act cases to the Special Court concerned.

details.text: In case of written information about a cognizable offence, attach an exact copy of the written complaint to the station record and send the original to Court with the FIR.

steps.title: Decline investigation for want of sufficient ground
steps.text: Where there is no sufficient ground for entering on an investigation, the SHO shall not investigate the case; he must record the reasons in his report, forward the daily diary report fortnightly to the Magistrate, and notify the informant of the decision not to investigate [Section 176 BNSS].
legal_basis: Section 176 BNSS 2023
Section 157(1)(b) CrPC (now BNSS 176) as printed in older sources
steps.deadline: Daily diary report forwarded to the Magistrate fortnightly [Section 176 BNSS]
steps.applies_when: No sufficient ground to enter on an investigation after registration
steps.triage_why: Applies only if the SHO decides NOT to investigate; this case involves serious POCSO/BNS offences where investigation is mandatory.

ticks.do: Do not investigate the case where there is no sufficient ground for entering on an investigation [Section 176 BNSS].
Record the reasons for not investigating in the SHO's report.
Forward the daily diary report fortnightly to the Magistrate.
Notify the informant of the decision not to investigate.

details.text: Make a note in the General Diary with detailed reasoning when deciding not to investigate.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: An FIR once started shall on no account be cancelled — not by the officer in charge, a Magistrate/Judge or any other police officer; it can be concluded only by refusing investigation (Further Action Dropped), transfer to the jurisdictional station on the question of jurisdiction, transfer to a specialized agency (Crime Branch/CBI), or a final report (charge sheet, or refer report as False / Mistake of Fact / Mistake of Law / Civil Nature / FAD).

steps.title: Proceed to the spot after sending the report
steps.text: After sending the FIR report, proceed in person to the spot — or depute a subordinate officer of the prescribed rank — to investigate the facts and circumstances of the case and, if necessary, take measures for the discovery and arrest of the offender; the personal spot visit may be dispensed with where information as to the offence is given against a person by name and the case is not of a serious nature [Section 176 BNSS].
legal_basis: Section 176 BNSS 2023
steps.responsible: Station House Officer / deputed subordinate officer
steps.triage_why: Essential for crime scene processing and evidence collection (especially in a case involving a specific room/location).

ticks.do: Proceed in person to the spot after sending the FIR report, or depute a subordinate officer of the prescribed rank, to investigate the facts and circumstances of the case [Section 176 BNSS].
notes: The personal spot visit may be dispensed with where information as to the offence is given against a person by name and the case is not of a serious nature.

ticks.do: Take measures for the discovery and arrest of the offender if necessary.

details.text: If the offence is of a serious nature and the police department/Government/any law has prescribed the rank of the Investigating Officer, the case shall be investigated by the officer so designated.

conflicts.description: Condition for dispensing with the spot visit: bnss_2023 BNSS 176 (like the proviso (a) to Section 157(1) CrPC) allows the officer not to proceed in person where information is given against a person BY NAME and the case is not of a serious nature; kerala_police_sop_2020 p.26 prints the opposite condition — 'if the offence is not of serious nature and NO accused is named in the FIR, there is no need to cause immediate action (Section 157 CrPC)'.
conflicts.resolution: Law prevails: the canonical text uses the BNSS 176 condition (accused named + case not serious). The contradictory Kerala sentence is not carried as a detail, since a lower source may not change the requirement.

steps.title: Record rape victim's statement at her chosen place
steps.text: Record a rape victim's statement at her residence or a place of her choice, as far as practicable by a woman police officer, in the presence of her parents or guardian or near relatives or a social worker of the locality; the statement may be recorded by audio-video means, including on a mobile phone [Section 176 BNSS].
legal_basis: Section 176 BNSS 2023
steps.responsible: Woman police officer (as far as practicable)
steps.applies_when: Investigation of a rape case
steps.triage_why: Statutory requirement under Section 176 BNSS for sexual offences; failure to follow prescribed procedure for victim statements in POCSO/rape cases can jeopardize the prosecution.

ticks.do: Record a rape victim's statement at her residence or at a place of her choice, as far as practicable by a woman police officer.
Record the statement in the presence of her parents or guardian or near relatives or a social worker of the locality.
Consider recording the statement by audio-video means, including on a mobile phone.
notes: Section 176 BNSS permits audio-video recording but does not require it: the statement 'may' be so recorded.

details.text: In the case of women victims, the statement should preferably be recorded by a Woman Police Officer.

steps.title: Collect and videograph forensic evidence
steps.text: For offences punishable with seven years or more, have a forensic expert visit the crime scene to collect forensic evidence, and have the process videographed on a mobile phone or other electronic device (mandatory from the date notified by the State Government) [Section 176(3) BNSS].
legal_basis: Section 176(3) BNSS 2023
steps.applies_when: Offence punishable with imprisonment of 7 years or more
steps.triage_why: Statutory mandate under Section 176(3) BNSS for offences punishable by 7+ years (Rape/POCSO); failure to secure forensic evidence and videography is a procedural lapse that can defeat the case.

ticks.do: Ensure a forensic expert visits the crime scene to collect forensic evidence for offences punishable with seven years or more [Section 176(3) BNSS]
Videograph the forensic process on a mobile phone or other electronic device
notes: Mandatory from the date notified by the State Government [Section 176(3) BNSS]

details.text: Where the State lacks a forensic facility, the State Government must notify the use of another State's facility; the forensic-visit mandate takes effect from a date the State Government must notify within five years.

steps.title: Enter post-FIR proceedings in the Case Diary
steps.text: Note in the Case Diary all proceedings carried out by any police officer under the registration of the FIR: questioning of the victim, questioning of witnesses, search and seizure, medical examination, etc.
steps.triage_why: Case Diary entries are statutory requirements; omissions can lead to the evidence being deemed unreliable or inadmissible during trial.

ticks.do: Note in the Case Diary all proceedings carried out by any police officer under the registration of the FIR.
sub: Questioning of the victim
Questioning of witnesses
Search and seizure
Medical examination
Other such proceedings

steps.title: Publish the FIR online except in sensitive cases
steps.text: Upload the copy of the FIR on the police website within twenty-four hours of registration, unless the offence is sensitive in nature (sexual offences, offences pertaining to insurgency and terrorism and that category, POCSO Act offences and such other offences); the time may be extended up to forty-eight hours where there are connectivity problems due to geographical location or other unavoidable difficulty, and by a maximum of a further 72 hours only for connectivity problems due to geographical location [Supreme Court, Youth Bar Association of India, W.P.(Crl) No. 68/2016].
steps.deadline: Within 24 hours of registration (48 hours, plus a maximum further 72 hours, only for the stated connectivity difficulties)
steps.triage_why: The step explicitly exempts sexual offences and POCSO Act offences from the mandatory upload requirement.

ticks.do: Upload the copy of the FIR on the police website within twenty-four hours of registration [Supreme Court, Youth Bar Association of India, W.P.(Crl) No. 68/2016].
Withhold the upload where the offence is sensitive in nature, falling in any of the categories below.
sub: Sexual offences
Offences pertaining to insurgency and terrorism and that category
POCSO Act offences
Such other offences

ticks.do: Allow the time to be extended up to forty-eight hours where there are connectivity problems due to geographical location or other unavoidable difficulty.
Allow a maximum further extension of 72 hours only for connectivity problems due to geographical location.

details.text: The decision NOT to upload an FIR copy is taken by the Sub Divisional Police Officer concerned — in no case by an officer below the rank of Dy.SP/ASP — and must be duly communicated to the jurisdictional Magistrate.

details.text: On the CCTNS platform this is done through the Publish/Un-publish option: on clicking Yes in the Publish option the FIR gets published and becomes available on the State Police website for viewing and downloading by the public.

steps.title: Mirror cognizable information in the Station Diary
steps.text: As soon as the report has been entered in the FIR Book, briefly record the substance of the report in the police station General/Station Diary; all information relating to cognizable offences — whether resulting in registration of an FIR or leading to an enquiry — must be mandatorily and meticulously reflected in that Diary, and the decision to conduct a preliminary enquiry must also be reflected in it.
steps.triage_why: Mandatory administrative requirement to ensure the integrity of the FIR registration process and prevent allegations of delayed reporting.

ticks.do: Record briefly the substance of the report in the police station General or Station Diary as soon as the report has been entered in the FIR Book.
Reflect mandatorily and meticulously in that Diary all information relating to cognizable offences, whether it results in registration of an FIR or leads to an enquiry.
Reflect the decision to conduct a preliminary enquiry in that Diary also.

details.text: If the officer in charge receives a telegram, telephone message or rumour while in the police station, make an entry in the Station General Diary of the gist of the information he is proceeding to verify.

details.text: Register all FIRs through the CCTNS application and submit only the CCTNS-generated printout of the FIR to the Court; a General Diary entry is a must for registering an FIR in CCTNS; supervisory officers ensure SHO compliance.

details.text: When information regarding an incident, complaint or allegation is received, record the brief of that information in the General Diary without changing the material facts.

steps.title: Register only one FIR per incident
steps.text: Under no circumstances register more than one FIR in respect of one and the same incident; if there is more than one incident forming part of the same transaction, register only one FIR.
steps.triage_why: Sound legal practice to avoid multiplicity of proceedings, but a procedural error in registration usually doesn't defeat the prosecution of the underlying crime.

ticks.do: Do not register more than one FIR in respect of one and the same incident, under any circumstances.
Register only one FIR where there is more than one incident forming part of the same transaction.

details.text: A second FIR on the same incident is permissible only as a counter-case: not filed by the same person who filed the first FIR, and based on allegations different from those in the first FIR [P. Sreekumar v. State of Kerala (2018) 4 SCC 579]; if the accused in the first FIR comes forward with a different version or counter case on the same incident, conduct investigation on both FIRs.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: When two persons prefer complaints against each other, the officer in charge is bound, depending on the nature of the complaints, to register both cases; rival versions may be investigated by the same Investigating Officer and both cases should be tried by the same court; after due investigation, differentiate the aggrieved from the aggressor and file the charge sheet against the aggressor.

steps.title: Turn Out to the Scene and Render Aid
steps.text: Proceed in person to the spot, or depute a subordinate officer of the prescribed rank, to investigate the facts and take measures for the discovery and arrest of the offender (BNSS 176). The investigation team proceeds with the Investigation Kit and case-appropriate safety measures; after reaching the scene, provide first aid/medical attention to the injured.
legal_basis: BNSS 176
steps.applies_when: BNSS 176 permits the officer in charge NOT to proceed in person or depute a subordinate where the information is against a person by name and the case is not of a serious nature, and not to investigate at all where there is no sufficient ground; in either case the reasons must be stated in the report to the Magistrate.
steps.triage_why: Statutory duty to investigate and provide medical attention to an injured victim; failure to provide medical aid to an injured victim is a grave omission.

steps.title: Assess Scene Safety Before Entering
steps.text: Before entering, ensure there is no immediate threat to responders: scan the area for sights, sounds and smells that may present danger (e.g. gasoline, natural gas); if the situation involves a clandestine drug laboratory, biological weapons, or radiological/chemical threats, contact the appropriate specialist agency BEFORE entering. Approach the scene so as to reduce risk to officers while maximising the safety of victims, witnesses and others; survey for dangerous persons, control the situation, notify supervisory personnel and call for backup.
steps.triage_why: Safety protocol for hazardous materials (gas/bio-weapons) which is not applicable to the facts of this specific case.

steps.title: Control access and prevent scene contamination
steps.text: Establish a perimeter around the crime scene with police line tape and prevent anyone from entering, so that the scene and the evidence are not contaminated; limit access to people directly involved in scene processing and control the flow of personnel and animals entering and leaving. Establish and strictly follow designated entry/exit routes, use the safe route when moving through the scene and avoid disturbing it. Wear gloves and protective clothing/PPE to avoid contaminating evidence, and use disposable devices for collecting biological evidence. Maintain the privacy and confidentiality of the scene; do not allow media and press personnel.
steps.triage_why: Directly linked to preventing contamination of forensic evidence in a sexual offence case, which is critical for prosecution.

steps.title: Locate latent fingerprints before searching the scene
steps.text: Begin the search by locating the latent fingerprints before any item is touched or moved; direct the fingerprint expert indicating the areas to be examined; observe and describe all visible details before dusting anything for latent fingerprints.
legal_basis: Section 302 IPC [now BNS 103(1)] — punishment for murder: death, or imprisonment for life, and also liable to fine

Section 304B IPC [now BNS 80] — dowry death, where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for or in connection with any demand for dowry
Section 174 CrPC [now BNSS 194] — police to enquire and report on suicide etc.; report signed and forwarded forthwith to the District Magistrate or Sub-divisional Magistrate

Section 176 CrPC [now BNSS 196] — inquiry by Magistrate into cause of death; power to disinter and examine a body; relatives to be informed and allowed to remain present ('relative' means parents, children, brothers, sisters and spouse)
Section 327 IPC [now BNS 119(1)] — voluntarily causing hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act (imprisonment up to ten years and fine)
Section 323 IPC [now BNS 115(2)] — punishment for voluntarily causing hurt (except the case provided for by s.334 IPC): imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
Section 284 IPC [now BNS 286] — punishment for careless handling of poisonous substances

Sections 299, 302, 304A, 306, 307, 309, 324, 326, 328 and 489A IPC [now BNS 100, 103, 106(1), 108, 109, no direct BNS equivalent for 309 (BNS 226 covers only attempt to suicide to compel or restrain a public servant), 118(1), 118(2), 123 and 178 respectively] — offences relating to administration of poisonous substances
Poisons Act 1919; Drugs Act 1940; Drugs and Magic Remedies Act 1954; Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985; Pharmacy Act 1948 — possession, sale and control of poisons

Motor Vehicles Act 1988 — driving or attempting to drive with alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected by breath analyser, or under the influence of a drug so as to be incapable of exercising proper control over the vehicle
steps.triage_why: Sound forensic practice to collect latent prints, but the case primarily relies on biological and electronic evidence.

steps.title: Choose a Systematic Scene Search Pattern
steps.text: Search the scene by an orderly, recognised pattern so no material evidence is missed: Line/Strip method (large and outdoor scenes - walk end to end and return); Grid method (double line search, large scenes such as fields); Wheel/Ray method (small circular scenes - from the centre outward along radii); Spiral method (outdoor scenes without barriers - ever-widening circle from the core); Zone method (houses/buildings - divide into four quadrants and examine each).
steps.triage_why: Methodological approach to searching a scene; ensures thoroughness but the omission of a specific 'pattern' does not defeat the case if evidence is found.

ticks.do: Search the scene by an orderly, recognised pattern so no material evidence is missed.
sub: Line/Strip method (large and outdoor scenes - walk end to end and return).
Grid method (double line search, large scenes such as fields).
Wheel/Ray method (small circular scenes - from the centre outward along radii).
Spiral method (outdoor scenes without barriers - ever-widening circle from the core).
Zone method (houses/buildings - divide into four quadrants and examine each).

details.text: The most practical method is to begin the search at the point where the body is first discovered and extend the search in an outward direction until the entire room or location has been covered.

steps.title: Call the Forensic Expert Under BNSS 176(3)
steps.text: For every offence punishable with seven years or more, the officer in charge of the police station shall cause a forensic expert to visit the crime scene to collect forensic evidence, and shall cause videography of the process on a mobile phone or other electronic device (BNSS 176(3)); where the State lacks a forensic facility, the State Government notifies utilization of another State's facility.
legal_basis: BNSS 176(3)
steps.deadline: Mandatory from the date notified by the State Government, which must be notified as early as possible but not later than five years (BNSS 176(3))
steps.responsible: Officer in charge of the police station
steps.applies_when: Offence punishable with imprisonment of seven years or more
steps.triage_why: BNSS 176(3) makes forensic visit and videography mandatory for offences punishable by 7+ years; POCSO and BNS 64(2)(M) meet this threshold. Failure is a statutory breach.

ticks.do: Cause a forensic expert to visit the crime scene to collect forensic evidence for every offence punishable with seven years or more.
notes: Mandatory ('shall') on the officer in charge of the police station.

ticks.do: Cause videography of that process on a mobile phone or other electronic device (BNSS 176(3)).
Use another State's forensic facility as notified by the State Government where the State lacks a forensic facility.
notes: Mandatory from the date notified by the State Government, which must be notified as early as possible but not later than five years (BNSS 176(3)).

details.text: Role allocation: if only the police first responder is present/equipped, the first responder performs the scene photography/videography per SOP; if only the forensic team is present (fully equipped), it performs the recording; if both are functional and well equipped, the first responder records where there is a time lag in the forensic team reaching the scene, and where there is no time lag the forensic team takes the lead and performs the complete SOP.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Rationale: forensic experts are limited in number and stationed at district headquarters and delay disturbs the scene, so the first responder's own videography/photography preserves the scene authentically; specific and expert photography for better erudition of evidence follows, done by forensic science experts with distinct training.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: In heinous crime, call an FSL team comprising a Forensic Expert appropriate to the nature of the crime to the place of occurrence.

steps.title: Apply the Statutory Audio-Video Recording Contexts
steps.text: Know and apply the statutory contexts requiring audio-video recording: (1) BNSS 105 - search and seizure processes (mandatory); (2) BNSS 173 - FIR registration: for victims of BNS 64-71, 74-79 and 124 offences who are mentally/physically disabled, record the information at the informant's residence or chosen place in the presence of an interpreter/special educator, with videography of the recording MANDATORY; (3) BNSS 176 - rape victim's statement at her residence or place of choice, if possible by a woman police officer, optionally recordable by audio-video means including mobile phone; (4) BNSS 180 - witness statements may also be recorded by audio-video means (optional); (5) BNSS 185 - police search must compulsorily be recorded by audio-video means, desirably by mobile phone.
legal_basis: BNSS 105
BNSS 173(1)
BNSS 176
BNSS 180
BNSS 185
steps.triage_why: Provides legal context and definitions for when audio-video recording is required under BNSS; it is a guide for application rather than a discrete investigative step.

ticks.do: Know and apply the statutory contexts requiring audio-video recording.
sub: (1) BNSS 105 - search and seizure processes (mandatory).
(2) BNSS 173 - FIR registration for victims of BNS 64-71, 74-79 and 124 offences who are mentally or physically disabled, with videography of the recording MANDATORY.
(3) BNSS 176 - rape victim's statement at her residence or place of choice, if possible by a woman police officer, optionally recordable by audio-video means including mobile phone.
(4) BNSS 180 - witness statements, which may also be recorded by audio-video means (optional).
(5) BNSS 185 - police search, which must compulsorily be recorded by audio-video means, desirably by mobile phone.

ticks.do: Record the information under BNSS 173 at the informant's residence or the place chosen by the informant, in the presence of an interpreter or special educator.

details.text: The crime scene itself is to be recorded through any audio-video electronic means, preferably mobile phone - a major change of the new criminal laws to improve evidence quality, overcome contradictory witness testimony and defeat allegations of tampering.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Searches under BNSS s.85 (proclamation and attachment chapter) are also to be recorded through audio-video electronic means, preferably mobile phone, in addition to s.105 and s.185 searches.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Where the person making a statement is temporarily or permanently mentally or physically disabled, the Magistrate takes the assistance of an interpreter or special educator and the statement shall also be recorded by audio-video electronic means, preferably mobile phone (BNSS s.183(6)); the recorded statements are entered in the case diary.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: The IO may record witness statements by audio-video electronic means as he deems fit in the interest of investigation; the audio-video clips will be part of the case diary.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: For orders as to custody and disposal of property pending trial (BNSS s.497(3)), a photograph of the property is MANDATORY and a videograph on mobile phone or any electronic media is OPTIONAL.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: AV recording also extends across the wider procedural tree: statements before the Magistrate u/s 183(1) BNSS including confession of the accused in the presence of an advocate; recording of identification parade u/s 54 BNSS (by jailor or court staff, since police presence is not allowed); property custody/disposal and Malkhana disposal proceedings u/s 497; identifying stolen property; and voice sampling.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Apply the same procedures and do's/don'ts across the investigative tree after FIR registration: oral evidence u/s 180(1) BNSS; documentary evidence u/s 176(3) BNSS (scene overview, crime scene map/Naksha Mauka, SOC recording of body/weapons/other evidence, and counter-verification of scene and recovery in the presence of the accused/Tasdeek Naksha Mauka); digital evidence seized; evidence before the Magistrate; and other prosecutory evidence (voice sample, narco analysis).
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: When videographing a statement, ensure no one other than the person who has to witness the statement is present in the area, and set up a close-up frame for recording the subject/witness.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Where the person making the statement is temporarily or permanently mentally or physically disabled, the Magistrate shall take the assistance of an interpreter or a special educator in recording the statement; the statement shall also be recorded through audio-video electronic means, preferably mobile phone; enter the recorded statements in the case diary.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

steps.title: Record Grounds and Film the BNSS 185 Search
steps.text: Before a police search under BNSS 185, record in writing in the case diary the grounds of belief and specify, so far as possible, the thing for which the search is to be made; the search itself must compulsorily be recorded by audio-video electronic means, desirably by mobile phone.
legal_basis: BNSS 185
steps.triage_why: BNSS 185 mandates recording grounds of belief in the case diary and compulsory audio-video recording of the search. Omission can invalidate the search and seizure.

Specify, so far as possible, the thing for which the search is to be made.

steps.title: Adopt e-SAKSHYA as the Default Recording Tool
steps.text: The Investigating Officer must download the e-SAKSHYA application on his own mobile phone and must compulsorily use it for all audio-video recording; a mobile or other recorder may be used ONLY where recording in e-SAKSHYA is not possible for technical reasons (and then only with the prescribed fallback safeguards).
steps.triage_why: The use of e-SAKSHYA is a compulsory procedural requirement for electronic evidence integrity under current BNSS guidelines.

ticks.do: Download the e-SAKSHYA application on the Investigating Officer's own mobile phone.
Use e-SAKSHYA compulsorily for all audio-video recording.
Use a mobile or other recorder ONLY where recording in e-SAKSHYA is not possible for technical reasons.
notes: Permissive - such alternative recording is allowed only with the prescribed fallback safeguards.

details.text: App-based recording embeds latitude and longitude, date and time automatically from GPS as metadata; the crime number and other details are entered manually by the user; the smartphone calculates the hash value of each file in real time.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Each photo/video file carries its metadata in the file itself, the real-time hash is embedded in the metadata (and may even be printed on the photo/video), and the file syncs immediately to a secure server or is emailed to a specified address (server address and email ID also stored in metadata) - maintaining authenticity and chain of custody; NCRB's e-Sakshya is cloud-based and is being dovetailed into CCTNS-2.0.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: MEITY may notify that photo/video captured through the standardized application will not require external certification, the system-generated hash/timestamp report sufficing for s.63(4) BSA; e-Sakshya uses blockchain technology for data integrity.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

conflicts.resolution: The binding Gujarat requirement governs: e-SAKSHYA on the IO's own mobile is the default recording instrument in Gujarat. The BPRD departmentally-approved-device specification is retained only as the equipment standard for the camera/AV-recorder stream, i.e. where e-SAKSHYA is technically unavailable or where a dedicated camera is used in addition.

steps.title: Check Equipment and Conditions Before Recording
steps.text: Before recording, ensure: the phone/recorder is in working order and fully charged (keep a power bank against low battery); proper lighting is arranged; recording of every crime-related place and article is done from a proper angle and is clearly visible; and care is exercised for weather conditions.
steps.triage_why: These are best practices for quality control. While important for clarity, a slightly dark video does not automatically defeat a prosecution if the evidence is otherwise authenticated.

ticks.do: Ensure the following are in place before recording.
sub: The phone or recorder is in working order and fully charged.
A power bank is kept against low battery.
Proper lighting is arranged.
Recording of every crime-related place and article is done from a proper angle and is clearly visible.
Care is exercised for weather conditions.

details.text: Verify the audio-video recording equipment is operational, inform all parties present about the recording process, and use a tripod or stabilizer to prevent shaky footage.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Equipment standard: use a departmentally approved and issued device (min. 3.0 MP / 3.2 MP gross, on-camera viewer, close-up capability, flash and a sterile removable memory card or device of at least 8 to 16 MB). At the start of each tour of duty confirm the device works, has a clean memory card and fully charged batteries, carry a 90-degree evidence ruler (white, grey and black planes) for injury close-ups, set the date stamp correctly but so it will NOT print on the images, and set exposure, flash and focus to 'automatic' with storage control at 'best quality'.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Calibrate the time and location settings of the camera before starting the recording; carry spare blank memory cards; ensure maximum battery charge and carry connecting wires for direct charging/operating of the camera.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: For an audio-video recorder, insert a fresh read-only flash device and format it before performing the recording.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Take on record that the memory card was blank before any recording.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Aide-memoir: store the recording on an external memory card/storage device alone, or on cloud storage, or on both (parallel storage), setting the input file path preferably to the removable media/MMC card or the cloud server per protocol; note the file size for one or more scene locations.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

steps.title: Involve Two Independent Panchas on Camera
steps.text: Keep at least two independent witnesses (panchas) present for every search/seizure. Have the panchas look towards the camera, give their own introduction, and declare that the search/seizure proceedings are being carried out in their presence, stating case number, police station, date and time; the witnesses must sign the seizure list on camera.
legal_basis: BNSS 105
steps.triage_why: Independent witnesses (panchas) and their on-camera verification are critical for the legality of search/seizure and to prevent allegations of planting evidence.

The common requirement in both sources - that the witnesses append their signatures on the seizure memo/list - is retained.

steps.title: Open the Recording With Formal Introductions
steps.text: At the beginning of the recording, the Investigating Officer must look towards the camera and give his own introduction - name, designation, case number, police station, proceedings being commenced, date and time - and, in the presence of the two witnesses, state their names, addresses and the purpose of their presence.
steps.triage_why: Proper identification of the officer and witnesses on record is essential to establish the chain of custody and the authenticity of the proceedings.

ticks.do: Look towards the camera at the beginning of the recording and give your own introduction as the Investigating Officer.
sub: Name.
Designation.
Case number.
Police station.
Proceedings being commenced.
Date and time.

ticks.do: State, in the presence of the two witnesses, their names, addresses and the purpose of their presence.

details.text: Include date, time, location, case details and warrant details in the introduction; as far as possible record latitude-longitude and time of recording along with the video; the video recording so made shall be part of the case diary.

steps.title: Enforce Silence During Recorded Proceedings
steps.text: During recording of search/seizure/statement proceedings, instruct all persons present to keep their phones in silent mode and not to make unnecessary noise so the audio is clear and undisturbed; all team members of the first responder or forensic team and the witnesses present must maintain silence and avoid chatter or loose talk which the defence could use against the investigative sanctity.
steps.triage_why: Maintaining silence is sound practice to avoid defense arguments regarding 'coaching' or 'interference', but is not a statutory mandate.

ticks.do: Instruct all persons present during recording of search, seizure or statement proceedings to keep their phones in silent mode.
Instruct all persons present not to make unnecessary noise so the audio is clear and undisturbed.
Require all team members of the first responder or forensic team and the witnesses present to maintain silence.
Avoid chatter or loose talk which the defence could use against the investigative sanctity.

details.text: BPRD's own formulation of the discipline: never talk while shooting the video or capturing photographs at the crime scene, keep the audio of the recorder off and turn off the mic devices of the officials present.

conflicts.description: bprd_av_recording_sop (bprd-av-recording-procedures p.39) directs that the officer never talk while shooting, that the recorder's audio be OFF and that officials' mics be turned off; guj_cid_29_sops_2024 SOP 9 (p.38) mandates spoken on-camera introductions by the IO and by the panchas and a spoken concluding statement, and requires the audio recording to be clear and undisturbed, while BPRD itself (bprd-av-recording-procedures p.39) requires the officer to narrate the discovery and seizure of each item.
conflicts.resolution: Binding Gujarat governs: audio must be ON and the spoken introduction, item-by-item seizure narration and concluding statement are mandatory. The BPRD audio-off/no-talk rule is not adopted as such; it survives only as the requirement that no extraneous talk, chatter or commentary occur during silent scene-documentation footage, which is what the Gujarat noise-discipline rule independently requires.

steps.title: Close the recording with a concluding statement
steps.text: After the search is completed, show the panchas on camera and, in their presence, give a concluding statement on the recording - name, designation, case number, police station, panchas' names and addresses, and completion date and time; STOP the recording only after this concluding statement (a summary of the search and seizure operation).
steps.triage_why: A concluding statement on camera ensures the recording is complete and prevents claims that the video was edited or truncated.

steps.title: Document Each Stage of the Search on Camera
steps.text: Document the search process methodically on the recording: cover each room or area in sequence with a detailed walkthrough; capture close-ups of seized items showing their condition and identifying marks; clearly narrate the discovery and seizure of each item, ensuring it is visible in frame; record the process of recovery with close-up videography revealing identifiable details; and record the preparation of the seizure list and its signing by the witnesses.
legal_basis: BNSS 105
steps.triage_why: Methodical documentation of the recovery process is essential to prove the location and condition of evidence (e.g., the room where the offence occurred).

steps.title: Keep the audio-video record unbroken throughout
steps.text: Record the whole episode continuously from start to finish, without any break or unnecessary interruption; include a starting shot and an ending shot describing the starting and ending points of the recording. If the search will be prolonged beyond the capacity of one memory card, run two audio-video recordings in parallel so continuity is maintained - the card change is captured on the spare device - and preserve that recording along with the main memory card.
steps.triage_why: Continuity of recording is required to prevent allegations of tampering or 'selective editing' of the evidence.

steps.title: Review, Store and Label the Recording
steps.text: Immediately after recording: review the recording/photographs on the device's own screen for accuracy and completeness; do NOT delete any photographically faulty images at the scene; do NOT view the files on any device that would enable editing (memory card reader or computer); record the device's assigned image numbers for the case; note in the incident report that photographs/video were taken of the victim and of the scene; securely store and back up the recording; and label it with date, time, location, case details and a brief description of the content. Do not submit unclear photographs or recordings to the court.
steps.triage_why: Preventing editing and recording image numbers is critical for the admissibility of electronic evidence under the Indian Evidence Act/BSA.

details.text: Don'ts: do not disturb the crime scene before taking photographs and video; do not submit unclear photographs and recordings to the court; do not submit digital evidence without the certificate under BSA s.63(4)(c); do not forget to mention the hash value of each individual photograph and video in the case diary. The SOP is not exhaustive - present the original crime scene to the competent court through every possible mode and tool including digital photographs and video footage.

steps.title: Establish Positions by Photographing an Undisturbed Scene
steps.text: Photograph and videotape the scene as the FIRST part of crime scene documentation, BEFORE touching, moving or handling anything; obtain photographs of the scene from a number of angles so the exact position of the object, the body (if any) and the weapons can later be established. Take photographs and video of the crime scene both before and after any alteration.
steps.triage_why: Crime scene evidence (especially in sexual offences) is highly degradable. Documentation before alteration is essential to preserve the scene's integrity.

steps.title: Photograph the Scene, Body and Each Exhibit
steps.text: Photograph/videograph in three ranges: (1) overall wide-angle coverage of the whole scene and the surrounding area (for outdoor scenes drone cameras may be used); (2) mid-range/orientation shots showing the relation and location of each piece of evidence to the others and to its surroundings; (3) close-up/macro shots of each item taken TWICE - once WITH a scale/ruler and once WITHOUT - so the defence cannot allege the scene was altered or that anything was concealed. Photograph the dead body (if present) to show location, injuries and condition; photograph each piece of evidence where found to establish its relationship to the victim; shoot evidence from straight above to eliminate distance distortion; and photograph blood patterns with a scale from different angles.
steps.triage_why: Using scales and specific ranges is professional forensic practice that strengthens the case, but the absence of a ruler does not inherently invalidate the evidence.

ticks.do: Photograph or videograph in three ranges.
sub: (1) Overall wide-angle coverage of the whole scene and the surrounding area.
(2) Mid-range or orientation shots showing the relation and location of each piece of evidence to the others and to its surroundings.
(3) Close-up or macro shots of each item taken TWICE, once WITH a scale or ruler and once WITHOUT.
notes: For outdoor scenes drone cameras may be used.
The paired close-ups prevent the defence alleging that the scene was altered or that anything was concealed.

ticks.do: Photograph the dead body to show location, injuries and condition.

details.text: In cases of murder or suicide a medical officer should accompany the police to the scene whenever possible and inspect the body and its surroundings before they are disturbed.
details.citation: Directorate of Forensic Science Services, Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt of India - Standard Operating Procedure for Crime Scene Investigation

details.text: Take colour photographs (colour photography is mandatory in UAPA cases); point the photographs at the evidence in the scene (tyre marks, footprints, perishable evidence); take long-distance shots to show the location (a drone may be utilized in certain cases), intermediate-distance shots to show relative positions, and close-up shots of injuries, footprints, dagger, firearms etc.; prefer the Department Photographer/Videographer, else private photographers at Government-fixed rates; in police encounter death cases photography/videography by BOTH private and department photographers is mandatory.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Scales/measuring tapes may be used while taking photographs from short distances.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Ensure proper lighting; take a complete set of pictures - aerial, long-range, mid-range and close-ups; include entry and exit routes, victims and evidence as far as possible; photograph/video transient marks such as blood stains, fingerprints and footprints as soon as possible; work from the exterior to the interior and from general to specific focus; prefer close-up photography for footprints, fingerprints, shoeprints, tyre tracks and injuries; take photographs and video with a scale when appropriate.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: When photographing injuries hold the camera at a 90-degree angle to the injury and take (1) a general-scene or full-frame photo/video of the person, (2) a shot showing the relationship of the injury to the subject's body, and (3) a close-up of the injury WITH and WITHOUT the evidence ruler.
details.citation: BPR&D - SOP on Audio-Video Recording under the New Criminal Laws (BNSS/BSA)

details.text: Give proper attention to the quality of videography/photography so it can be used for comparison purposes or to calculate precise measurements - latent prints, exemplars/standards, other ridge detail impressions, bloodstains, bullet strikes, transfer patterns, tool marks, bite marks, pattern injuries, and tire or footwear impressions.

steps.title: Draw and Annotate the Crime Scene Sketch
steps.text: Prepare a crime scene sketch - generally rough, but in heinous crimes also to scale: measure distances accurately and leave nothing of importance out; show the exact position of one or two permanent fixtures to help ascertain distances to major articles, exhibits and marks (blood stains, vehicle track marks); note the relationship of the various pieces of evidence to the surroundings; indicate the compass north point obtained by compass; and mention the title, case reference, date, time, and name and signature of the IO in the corner.
steps.triage_why: A sketch is a supporting document to the photographs and testimony; while helpful for the court, it is not a statutory requirement that would defeat the prosecution if missing.

ticks.do: Prepare a crime scene sketch, generally rough, but in heinous crimes also to scale.
Measure distances accurately and leave nothing of importance out.
Show the exact position of one or two permanent fixtures to help ascertain distances to major articles, exhibits and marks (blood stains, vehicle track marks).
Note the relationship of the various pieces of evidence to the surroundings.
Indicate the compass north point obtained by compass.
Mention in the corner the title, case reference, date, time, and name and signature of the IO.

details.text: The IO's sketch map is relevant under ss.7 & 9 Evidence Act [now BSA] as based on actual spot observation; record the scale, indicate direction, and have the person who prepares it sign it (two independent witnesses may be cited); the services of revenue officials may be sought; draw it on good quality A3/A4 paper; establish the scene boundary mentioning distances from identifying fixed points/pillars/marks.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Never avoid making a sketch in cases such as road accident, murder and gunshot fire; include the relative positions of objects, fittings, fixtures, furniture, vehicle, dead body and weapons, and mention road, wall, river, well, building, railway track and trees; measure exact inter-distances with a tape and do not rely on approximation; North should be toward the top shown by an arrow head; indicate identity marks such as tattoo, injuries and other atypical marks on the body as figures; always mention case number, section, police station, date, time and place of occurrence.
details.citation: Director, Forensic Science Laboratory, UP Police - Crime Scene (Protocol) Management (English section)

details.text: Always use appropriate and conventional symbols, letters and digits of a legend to avoid crowding the sketch.
details.citation: Director, Forensic Science Laboratory, UP Police - Crime Scene (Protocol) Management (English section)

details.text: Draw the site plan of the place of occurrence correctly, indicating the directions from where the accused persons came and left, the surrounding areas of the scene of crime, where the incident took place, from where the exhibits were lifted, and the source of light during night. If the scene of crime, the place where the accused in the vehicle were last seen, or any other relevant exhibits are at different locations, prepare separate site plans.
details.citation: Delhi Police Academy - Compendium of Scenarios for Investigating Officers, 2024

details.text: Prepare the demarcation memo of the place of occurrence, the site plan of the place of occurrence and the site plan of the place of recovery.

details.text: Show the point of source of light in the site plan of the place of occurrence if the same was prepared in the night.
