steps.title: Authorise Every Search by Warrant or Statute
steps.text: Treat search as an effective tool of investigation while recognising that it is a serious invasion of the liberty of a person. Conduct every search either under a warrant issued by a competent court (searches under Sections 93, 94, 95 and 97 CrPC as printed [now Sections 96, 97, 98 and 100 BNSS]) or, without warrant, only as authorised by the Code or a special Act (Sections 103, 165 and 166 CrPC as printed; for police searches during investigation, Sections 165 and 166 [now Sections 185 and 186 BNSS]). In all circumstances follow the general search provisions (Section 100 CrPC [now Section 103 BNSS]) together with the police-search provision (Section 165 CrPC [now Section 185 BNSS]).
legal_basis: BNSS 96
BNSS 103
BNSS 185
BNSS 186
steps.triage_why: General legal principle and guidance on the nature of searches.

notes: For police searches during investigation the provisions are Sections 165 and 166 [now Sections 185 and 186 BNSS].

details.text: Searches may be conducted before or after registration of the First Information Report; after the arrest of the accused; after confession; to collect evidence during investigation; on the orders of the Court; or for the maintenance of public peace and order.

details.text: Objects of a search: (a) arrest of a person concealing his presence; (b) recovery of property from arrested offenders to connect them with the offence, or of a weapon; (c) obtaining an article or thing wanted in a case; (d) a person wrongfully confined or missing; (e) discovery of firearms, explosives or other material for prevention and detection of crimes; (f) clues and evidence needed for the investigation.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Certain special and local Acts, such as the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, prescribe separate search-and-seizure procedures which the IO must follow in those cases.

details.text: Carry out searches always in strict conformity with law; fully comply with the provisions of Sections 94, 165, 166, 100, 101, 102 and 103 CrPC (as printed in the source).

details.text: Any police officer who seizes property, detains a person in custody, conducts a search or arrests a person illegally, for causing annoyance and without reasonable cause, commits a punishable offence (Section 116, Kerala Police Act, as printed — a state provision cited for the principle).

steps.title: Film the Search and Forward the Recording
steps.text: Record the entire process of conducting the search and of taking possession of any property, article or thing — including the preparation of the list of things seized and the signing of that list by the witnesses — through audio-video electronic means, preferably a mobile phone, and forward the recording without delay to the District Magistrate, Sub-divisional Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class. This applies to every Chapter VII BNSS search/seizure and every Section 185 BNSS investigation search.
legal_basis: BNSS 105
BNSS 185
steps.deadline: Forward the recording to the DM, SDM or JMFC without delay (Section 105 BNSS)
steps.responsible: Investigating Officer / police officer conducting the search
steps.triage_why: BNSS mandates audio-video recording of searches and seizures. Failure to record the process electronically is a statutory lapse that can jeopardize the validity of the seizure.

conflicts.description: bnss_2023 BNSS 105 (and guj_cid_29_sops_2024 SOP 9 p.36, and bprd_av_recording_sop bprd-av-legal-framework p.11) require forwarding 'without delay'; bprd_av_recording_sop (bprd-av-recording-procedures p.60) sets an outer limit of 'without delay, but not later than 48 hours'.
conflicts.resolution: The law's 'without delay' is the canonical requirement; the 48-hour figure is retained only as the national-advisory administrative outer bound and cannot dilute the statutory standard.

conflicts.description: tripura_sop_bundle (tripura-ndps, p.1) treats videography of the search and seizure as discretionary ('Preferably videograph the entire process of search and seizure'), while bnss_2023 BNSS 105 and delhi_compendium_2024 (Scenario 18, p.164) treat it as mandatory.
conflicts.resolution: The law layer governs: recording is mandatory under BNSS 105. The Tripura 'preferably' reflects the pre-BNSS position and is retained only as a lower-authority variant; it does not reduce the obligation.

steps.title: Call Independent Witnesses to Every Section 185 Search
steps.text: The general search provisions of Section 103 BNSS — independent witnesses, the search list and the rest — apply to every search made under Section 185 BNSS. Accordingly, before searching, call two or more independent and respectable inhabitants of the locality in which the place to be searched is situated (or of any other locality if an inhabitant of that locality is unavailable or unwilling) to attend and witness the search, and issue them a written order to do so if needed (the two-witness rule and the written order as printed in the state SOP under Section 100(4) CrPC [now BNSS 103(4)]).
legal_basis: BNSS 185
BNSS 103(4)
steps.triage_why: The presence of independent witnesses and the preparation of a search list under Section 103 BNSS are fundamental legal requirements for a valid search.

ticks.do: Apply the general search provisions of Section 103 BNSS, including independent witnesses and the search list, to every search made under Section 185 BNSS.

details.text: Insist on the witnesses being present throughout the search; when an article or document is discovered, draw the witnesses' attention to all the circumstances relating to it.

steps.title: Submit to Search and Control the Premises
steps.text: Before entering the house, the Investigating Officer and the search witnesses should submit their persons for search by the occupant of the house or some person on his behalf, and that person should be permitted to be present during the search. During the search permit no other person to enter or approach the house except a member of the household, and have the search party take charge of all telephones immediately on reaching the house.
steps.applies_when: Search of a house or other premises
steps.triage_why: Standard operating procedure for search integrity, but failure to submit to search does not typically defeat a prosecution if the search itself is legal.

steps.title: Respect the Occupant's Rights During the Search
steps.text: Ensure the legal rights of the person whose premises are searched are respected, since any violation may affect the search adversely. The occupant has the right: (a) to see the warrant of authorization duly signed and sealed by the issuing authority; (b) to verify the identity of each member of the search party; (c) to have at least two respectable and independent residents of the locality as witnesses; (d) to have a personal search of all members of the search party before commencement and at conclusion of the search; (e) to ensure that a personal search of females is carried out by another female only, with strict regard to decency; (f) to have a copy of the search list together with all annexures, for which acknowledgment should be given; (g) to call a medical practitioner if required; and (h) to have the facility of having meals etc. at the normal time.
steps.triage_why: Violation of statutory rights during search can lead to the evidence being declared inadmissible or the search being ruled illegal.

steps.title: Prepare and Sign the Search List On the Spot
steps.text: Prepare the search list — the list of the things seized in the course of the search — and have it signed by the search witnesses; Section 105 BNSS requires the preparation of that list and its signing by the witnesses to be captured in the audio-video recording, and the Section 103 BNSS general provisions govern the list itself. Prepare it on the spot during the search, in the prescribed search-list form, indicating the proceedings of the search and the documents and articles seized, and give a copy to the occupant of the premises under acknowledgement.

BNSS 105
steps.deadline: Prepare the search list on the spot, during the search (state SOP para 7.7, Section 100 CrPC [now BNSS 103] procedure); its preparation and signing must be audio-video recorded under Section 105 BNSS
steps.triage_why: Section 103 and 105 BNSS mandate the search list and audio-video recording; failure to comply is a statutory violation affecting the legality of the seizure.

steps.title: Record Every Element in the Search Memo
steps.text: While drawing up the search/seizure memo, record every element needed to prove the recovery: the name, occupation, age and address of each witness; the time, date and place of start of the proceedings; the reason for the search and the authority for it; a graphic description of the search operation in simple plain language (who opened the suitcase, who had the key, from where the incriminating documents or contraband were recovered and how they were concealed); and the date and time of conclusion of the search, recorded before leaving the place of search.
steps.responsible: Investigating Officer / officer writing the memo
steps.triage_why: Detailed memos strengthen the chain of custody and recovery proof, but minor omissions in description are usually curable in court.

details.text: Mention where and how the weighing of contraband goods was done, giving gross weight and net weight; mention the value of the contraband to be seized; and mention the number of samples drawn with their weight and identification marks.

details.text: Indicate the location from which the contraband exhibits, samples and documents proposed to be seized/taken over were recovered.

details.text: Give a copy of the memo/search list to the person whose premises were searched and obtain his receipt with date and time; to ensure proper identification, mention the complete description of the property seized in the memo.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: For recovery from or seizure of a vehicle: mention its registration number, colour, engine number, chassis number and model; if any part such as wheels, battery or lights is missing, note it in the memo.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: For firearms: mention the make (country made or foreign make), number and any specific writings inscribed on it; prepare a sketch of the recovered arms at the spot and mention in the memo that the sketch has been prepared; seal the arms and mention the mark of the seal in the seizure memo itself.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: For arms like knives, mention complete details in the memo, i.e. the length and breadth of the blade and of the handle.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: For stolen property such as ornaments and watches, mention special marks of identification and weight; mention special identification marks on articles including cloth, and if an article is used, torn or worn out, record that in the memo.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: For recoveries made from a field (a pit) etc., mention the depth dug up; the spot may be photographed and mention of this made in the recovery/seizure memo. For animals recovered, mention their complete description including any deformity.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: For currency notes recovered in trap cases registered under Section 5(ii) of the Prevention of Corruption Act (as printed), mention the number, denomination and serial numbers of the notes.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Where property is sealed for purposes of identification, record in the memo the handing over of the seal to one of the witnesses of the recovery/seizure, and refer to it in that witness's statement recorded under Section 161 CrPC [now BNSS 180].
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

steps.title: Collect Electronic Evidence by a Lawful Route
steps.text: Collect electronic/digital evidence with care and caution, following all legal procedure, in one of two ways: (1) by search and seizure under Sections 185 and 106 BNSS and Section 23 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, or (2) by causing production through summons/order under Section 94 BNSS.
legal_basis: BNSS 94
BNSS 106
BNSS 185
BSA 23
steps.triage_why: Electronic evidence (photos/recordings) is central to this case; failure to follow BNSS and BSA procedures renders the evidence inadmissible.

ticks.do: Collect electronic and digital evidence with care and caution, following all legal procedure, in one of two ways.
sub: (1) Search and seizure under Sections 185 and 106 BNSS and Section 23 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam.
(2) Production through summons or order under Section 94 BNSS.
notes: Duty of the Investigating Officer.

details.text: Electronic records/digital evidence are one form of documentary evidence: output produced from a computer system, whether printed on paper or stored in a CD/DVD, pen-drive, memory card, etc.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: 'Computer output' covers e-mail, server logs, documents, messages, websites, local evidence, voice mail messages, photos and videos, etc., including information stored, recorded or copied in semiconductor memory or other electronic information generated by a computer, communication device or any other device.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Voice evidence is mostly recorded/stored in various electronic devices which can function independently or attached to computer systems; handle the audio evidence, audio recording and storage devices like digital evidence.
details.citation: LNJN National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Science, MHA - A Forensic Guide for Crime Investigators: Standard Operating Procedures (marked Restricted)

details.text: The evidences of electronic records of conversations were regulated in accordance with the provisions in the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act (1885) as printed in the source [telegraph/wireless telegraphy statutes are now replaced by the Telecommunications Act, 2023]; with the enactment of the IT Act (2000) and the availability of electronic and digital technologies, the audio-video recorded evidences are to be collected in accordance with the provisions of that Act.

steps.title: Produce the Section 63 BSA Certificate
steps.text: Whenever electronic records are to be produced as evidence in a legal proceeding, produce with them the certificate under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam: Part-A (Annexure-1) signed by the person/party having charge of the computer or communication device, or by the person managing the activities concerned, and Part-B (Annexure-2) signed by the expert — each identifying the device and stating the hash value with its algorithm. Where Section 63 BSA has been complied with, electronic or digital records have the very same legal effect and enforceability as any other documents and are admissible without further proof or production of the original.
steps.responsible: Investigating Officer; person having lawful charge of the device (Part-A); Expert (Part-B)
steps.applies_when: Electronic records (in particular secondary computer output) are to be produced in evidence
steps.triage_why: Section 63(4)(c) BSA certificate is a mandatory statutory requirement for the admissibility of electronic records in court.

ticks.do: Produce the certificate under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam whenever electronic records are to be produced as evidence in a legal proceeding.
sub: Part-A (Annexure-1) signed by the person or party having charge of the computer or communication device, or by the person managing the activities concerned.
Part-B (Annexure-2) signed by the expert.

ticks.do: Ensure each Part identifies the device and states the hash value with its algorithm.
Rely on compliance with Section 63 BSA to give electronic or digital records the very same legal effect and enforceability as any other documents.
notes: Such records are then admissible without further proof or production of the original.

details.text: Admissibility [s.63(1) BSA]: information in an electronic record generated by a computer or other communication means, or stored/recorded/copied in electronic form, printed on paper, or stored/noted/copied in optical or magnetic media or semiconductor memory ('computer output'), shall be treated as a document and, if the Section 63 conditions are satisfied, is admissible as evidence without any further proof or production of the original.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Condition (a) [s.63(2) BSA]: the computer output containing the information was produced during the period in which the computer/communication means was regularly used for creating, storing or processing information for the purposes of regularly carrying on activities by a person having lawful control over its use.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Conditions (b)-(d) [s.63(2) BSA]: during that period, information of the kind contained in the electronic record (or of the kind from which it is derived) was regularly fed into the computer in the ordinary course of the said activities; during the material part of that period the computer was operating properly, or any malfunction was not such as to affect the electronic records or the accuracy of their particulars; and the information contained in the electronic records is derived from information fed in in the ordinary course.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Multiple computers [s.63(3) BSA]: where more than one computer or communication means was used for creating, storing or processing the information — whether working independently, over a network or through an intermediary medium — they shall all be treated as one larger system and counted as one unit.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Input and output [s.63(5) BSA]: information can be sent into and received from a computer in various forms, directly or indirectly, with or without human intervention, using appropriate equipment; it is not necessary that the computer output be produced directly or only by appropriate equipment.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Section 63(4)(c) BSA 2023 reproduces, with certain modifications, the provision corresponding to Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Annexure-1 (Part-A) is filled and signed on solemn oath by the party having lawful control of the device: it identifies the device/source (computer/storage media, DVR, mobile, flash drive, CD/DVD, server, cloud, other), brand, model, colour, serial number, IMEI/UIN/UID/MAC/Cloud ID, ownership/maintenance/management/operation status and the proper-functioning declaration, plus the hash value with algorithm (SHA-1/SHA-256/MD5/other legally acceptable standard), with date, time (24-hour format) and place. The hash report is enclosed with the certificate.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Annexure-2 (Part-B) is filled and signed on solemn oath by the Expert: the same device identification details plus hash value and algorithm, with name, designation, signature, date, time and place.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Where a DVR cannot be sealed and a technician backup is taken instead, the Section 63(4)(c) BSA certificate must be obtained along with the backup (UP FSL corroboration of the certificate requirement).
details.citation: State Forensic Science Laboratory UP / Technical Services HQ, Lucknow - A Collection of Standard Operating Procedures for Crime Scene Investigation (pictorial, BNSS/BSA era) - TRANSLATED FROM HINDI

details.text: Treat the audio-video recording in electronic form as an 'electronic record' synonymous to documentary evidence, and ensure that the requirements of section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act [now BSA 63] are fulfilled.
details.citation: LNJN National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Science, MHA - A Forensic Guide for Crime Investigators: Standard Operating Procedures (marked Restricted)

steps.title: Obtain and Record the Hash Value at Seizure
steps.text: At the time of seizure, obtain the hash value of the electronic records and make a note of it in the case diary, so that the reliability of the information is preserved. Computing the hash value of electronic records is compulsory, and mentioning the hash value in the certificate under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam is compulsory.
legal_basis: BSA 63
steps.applies_when: Electronic records/digital devices are seized
steps.triage_why: Hash values are compulsory under BSA to prove the integrity of electronic evidence; without them, the evidence can be challenged as tampered.

ticks.do: Obtain the hash value of the electronic records at the time of seizure and make a note of it in the case diary, so that the reliability of the information is preserved.
Compute the hash value of the electronic records.
notes: Computing the hash value is compulsory.

ticks.do: Mention the hash value in the certificate under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam.
notes: Mentioning the hash value in that certificate is compulsory.

details.text: Make a forensic image and verify all the digital information by its hash value.
details.citation: State Forensic Science Laboratory UP / Technical Services HQ, Lucknow - A Collection of Standard Operating Procedures for Crime Scene Investigation (pictorial, BNSS/BSA era) - TRANSLATED FROM HINDI

details.text: Use write blockers so that there is no change in the original form of the evidence, and keep the digital information obtained in its original form secure.
details.citation: State Forensic Science Laboratory UP / Technical Services HQ, Lucknow - A Collection of Standard Operating Procedures for Crime Scene Investigation (pictorial, BNSS/BSA era) - TRANSLATED FROM HINDI

details.text: Note the make of the CD (and similar media) along with its serial number.
details.citation: State Forensic Science Laboratory UP / Technical Services HQ, Lucknow - A Collection of Standard Operating Procedures for Crime Scene Investigation (pictorial, BNSS/BSA era) - TRANSLATED FROM HINDI

details.text: Effect the authentication of the electronic record by the use of an asymmetric crypto system and hash function which envelope and transform the initial electronic record into another electronic record, using the most widely used hash functions in tune with international standards - SHA (Secure Hash Algorithm) and MD5 (Message Digest); the SHA-1 hash function is a set of cryptographic hash functions designed by the National Security Agency (NSA), USA, and in India the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (CDAC) has developed a similar system which can be used after due evaluation.
details.citation: LNJN National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Science, MHA - A Forensic Guide for Crime Investigators: Standard Operating Procedures (marked Restricted)

details.text: Calculate the first hash result at the time of the acquisition of the conversation recorded in the recording device, before the witnesses, using commercially available or open source software such as SHA-1 or MD5, and document the computed hash result.
details.citation: LNJN National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Science, MHA - A Forensic Guide for Crime Investigators: Standard Operating Procedures (marked Restricted)

steps.title: Classify Electronic Records as Primary or Secondary
steps.text: Classify every electronic record before production: where the very device in which the electronic record was generated (e.g., the DVR/NVR machine connected to the CCTV camera) is itself produced before the Court, treat its output as primary evidence (Section 57 BSA); where a copy of the computer output, or a copy of any part of it, is collected and produced before the Court (e.g., CCTV footage in a DVR/NVR copied onto a CD/DVD, pen drive or hard disk), treat it as secondary evidence (Section 58 BSA), which requires the Section 63 BSA certificate.
legal_basis: BSA 57
BSA 58
BSA 63
steps.triage_why: This is a legal classification rule (Primary vs Secondary evidence) used to determine how to present evidence, not a procedural step to be 'performed'.

ticks.do: Classify every electronic record before production.
Treat the output as primary evidence (Section 57 BSA) where the very device in which the electronic record was generated is itself produced before the Court.
notes: Example: the DVR/NVR machine connected to the CCTV camera.

ticks.do: Treat the record as secondary evidence (Section 58 BSA) where a copy of the computer output, or a copy of any part of it, is collected and produced before the Court.
notes: Example: CCTV footage in a DVR/NVR copied onto a CD/DVD, pen drive or hard disk.
Secondary evidence requires the Section 63 BSA certificate.

steps.title: Protect Electronic Records During Packaging and Transport
steps.text: Take necessary safety measures to prevent damage to or tampering with the electronic records — use device covers, anti-static bags, Faraday bags, etc., to keep the records safe during packaging and transport.
steps.applies_when: Seized digital exhibits are packaged and transported
steps.triage_why: Electronic evidence is volatile; failure to use Faraday bags or anti-static packaging can lead to data loss or remote wiping (degradation).

ticks.do: Take necessary safety measures to prevent damage to or tampering with the electronic records.
Use protective packaging to keep the records safe during packaging and transport.
sub: Device covers.
Anti-static bags.
Faraday bags.
notes: The list is illustrative, not exhaustive.

details.text: Transportation rules: do not bend any disk; place hard disks and circuit boards in anti-static bags; handle all equipment with extra care; place keyboard, leads, mouse and modems in the attached bag; keep all equipment away from magnetic sources like loudspeakers, heated seats and radiation.
details.citation: State Forensic Science Laboratory UP / Technical Services HQ, Lucknow - A Collection of Standard Operating Procedures for Crime Scene Investigation (pictorial, BNSS/BSA era) - TRANSLATED FROM HINDI

details.text: Place labels on them; place personal organizers in paper envelopes; do not place items under heavy objects; an electronic device like a mobile should be packed in containers to avoid direct contact of hot sealing wax while sealing the exhibits.
details.citation: State Forensic Science Laboratory UP / Technical Services HQ, Lucknow - A Collection of Standard Operating Procedures for Crime Scene Investigation (pictorial, BNSS/BSA era) - TRANSLATED FROM HINDI

details.text: Check if the device is stand alone or attached to a network; if the evidence is small and portable such as a cell phone, tablet or telephone interceptor, collect it in an anti-static bag.
details.citation: LNJN National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Science, MHA - A Forensic Guide for Crime Investigators: Standard Operating Procedures (marked Restricted)

details.text: Pack all digital evidence in anti-static packaging; only paper bags and envelopes, cardboard boxes and anti-static containers should be used for packaging digital evidence, and plastic materials must not be used to preserve digital evidence.
details.citation: LNJN National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Science, MHA - A Forensic Guide for Crime Investigators: Standard Operating Procedures (marked Restricted)

details.text: Ensure that all digital evidence is packed in a manner that will prevent it from being bent, scratched or otherwise deformed, and label all containers used to package and store digital evidence clearly and properly.

steps.title: Assemble the kit for collecting audio evidence
steps.text: Carry cameras (still and video), anti-static bag, bubble wrap and other packing material, paper bags and sturdy boxes, labels, permanent marking pen and notepads, gloves, and audio recorders/micro voice recorders/digital audio recorders/audio cassettes/mini audio cassettes and cable jacks; keep new CD-Rs, a write blocker and a reader ready for selective use in the collection of audio evidences.
legal_basis: Indian Evidence Act, 1872 s.65B — admissibility of electronic records, with certificate [now BSA 63]
Indian Evidence Act, 1872 s.65A — special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record [now BSA 62]
Indian Evidence Act, 1872 s.45A — opinion of Examiner of Electronic Evidence, who is also treated as an expert [now BSA 39(2)]
Indian Evidence Act, 1872 s.7 — facts which are the occasion, cause or effect of facts in issue [now BSA 5]
Indian Evidence Act, 1872 ss.62 and 63 — primary and secondary evidence [now BSA 57 and 58]; s.65 — cases in which secondary evidence relating to documents may be given [now BSA 60]

Information Technology Act, 2000 s.2(1)(t) 'electronic record'; s.3(2) authentication of electronic record by asymmetric crypto system and hash function; s.4 legal recognition of electronic records; s.79A Examiner of Electronic Evidence (reference Chapter XIIA, IT (Amendment) Act, 2008)
Criminal Procedure Code s.29A — 'electronic record' has the meaning assigned in clause (t) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Information Technology Act, 2000
Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act (1885) as printed in the source [telegraph/wireless telegraphy statutes now replaced by the Telecommunications Act, 2023]
Prevention of Corruption Act — trap case investigations

Ritesh Sinha v. State of UP and Anr. (Criminal Misc. Appl. 3272 of 2010, Allahabad High Court) and the split Supreme Court Double Bench, undecided as of 31/07/2015 per the source [the power to order a voice sample is now expressly conferred by BNSS s.349]
steps.applies_when: Where audio or voice evidence arises in the case - a questioned conversation, recorded call, or an audio recording/storage device at the scene - and speaker identification or voice comparison may be required.
steps.triage_why: Logistical preparation for the search; while important, the lack of a specific brand of bag doesn't defeat the prosecution if the evidence is secured.

steps.title: Identify What to Seize at a Digital Scene
steps.text: Seize every device and accessory of evidential value, grouped by purpose: for retrieval of the evidence itself — floppy disks, CDs, DVDs, SIM cards, memory cards and pen drives, the mobile phone, and external/removable hard drives; because they help the examination — manuals and computer software, the password paper, and keys and dongles; for comparison of printouts — the printers, printouts and printer papers; so that the system can be reconstructed — the CPU unit, all cables, the power supply unit, the external hard disk, dongles, modems, and the keyboard and mouse. Also search the crime scene for any other valuable evidence such as password paper, diaries and notebooks, and ask the user for any password and record it.
steps.applies_when: Digital devices are found at the scene
steps.triage_why: The case relies on electronic evidence (photos, call recordings). Failure to seize the source devices leads to loss of primary evidence and inability to prove authenticity.

ticks.do: Seize the following for retrieval of the evidence itself.
sub: Floppy disks, CDs and DVDs.
SIM cards, memory cards and pen drives.
The mobile phone.
External and removable hard drives.

ticks.do: Seize the following because they help the examination.
sub: Manuals and computer software.

ticks.do: Seize the following for comparison of printouts.

ticks.do: Seize the following so that the system can be reconstructed.
sub: The CPU unit.

details.text: Device-by-device evidential yield (items 1-7): CPU — may itself be proof of theft, forgery etc.; holds all files and information including deleted files and folders, recovered by forensic imaging and analysis. Display monitor (CRT/LCD/TFT) and mobile phone screens if switched on — record everything visible by video/photo and written description. Smart cards, dongles and biometric scanners — card information, user information and other information. Digital cameras — pictures, videos, sound, removable cartridge, time and date stamps. Handheld devices (printed 'Handled Devices': PDAs, electronic organizers, smart phones) — address book, appointment calendar, documents, email, phone book, text and voice messages, email passwords. Hard drives — store all the information. LAN card / NIC — yields the device's MAC address.
details.citation: State Forensic Science Laboratory UP / Technical Services HQ, Lucknow - A Collection of Standard Operating Procedures for Crime Scene Investigation (pictorial, BNSS/BSA era) - TRANSLATED FROM HINDI

details.text: Device-by-device evidential yield (items 8-16): modems, routers, hubs and switches — configuration files hold IP-address information. Servers — last log-in, emails exchanged, material downloaded, pages accessed. Network cables and connectors — trace back to the computers concerned and identify the types of device attached. Pagers — address information, text messages, phone numbers. Printers — number of prints last taken, usage logs with time/date, network identification information, and fingerprints. Removable storage media and devices — files in which evidence may be found. Scanners — the scanning capability can help prove the illegal activity. Telephones — names, text and voice messages, memos, passwords, phone numbers, caller identification data; some store appointment information and work as voice recorders. Copiers — documents in physical and electronic form, user log and time/date data.
details.citation: State Forensic Science Laboratory UP / Technical Services HQ, Lucknow - A Collection of Standard Operating Procedures for Crime Scene Investigation (pictorial, BNSS/BSA era) - TRANSLATED FROM HINDI

details.text: Device-by-device evidential yield (items 17-21): CD and DVD drives — files/data in which evidence may be found. Credit card skimmers — the magnetic-strip track holds cardholder information (card expiry date, user's address, credit card number, user's name). Digital/smart watches — address book, notes, appointment calendar, phone numbers, email. Fax machines — documents, phone numbers, send/receive logs, film cartridge. Keyboard and mouse — examine for finger marks/fingerprints.

steps.title: Equip the Party for a Digital Scene
steps.text: Carry the Digital Crime Scene Investigation Kit to any scene with digital devices: scene-securing and recording hardware, empty storage media, packaging (anti-static and Faraday bags), a non-magnetic toolkit, and the forensic software set — write blockers, converters/adapters, boot software, forensic imaging software and volatile-data collection software.
steps.responsible: Digital crime scene party / Investigating Officer
steps.applies_when: The scene involves digital/electronic devices (including CCTV/DVR)
steps.triage_why: Using a professional kit is sound practice to prevent data corruption, but the absence of a specific kit does not automatically invalidate the evidence if it is seized.

ticks.do: Carry the Digital Crime Scene Investigation Kit to any scene with digital devices.
sub: Scene-securing and recording hardware.
Empty storage media.
Packaging, including anti-static and Faraday bags.
A non-magnetic toolkit.
The forensic software set.

ticks.do: Include in the forensic software set the following items.
sub: Write blockers.
Converters and adapters.
Boot software.
Forensic imaging software.
Volatile-data collection software.

details.text: Kit hardware: tape to secure the crime scene (yellow tape); digital camera (DSLR); extra battery/power backup; video camera; note/sketch pad; empty storage media (portable USB hard disk and pen drive); labels/evidence markers; pen and marker; storage container; anti-static bag; Faraday bag; toolkit with non-magnetic screwdrivers, pliers, forceps, scissors, clips, pins and cutter; torch and magnifying glass; rubber gloves.
details.citation: State Forensic Science Laboratory UP / Technical Services HQ, Lucknow - A Collection of Standard Operating Procedures for Crime Scene Investigation (pictorial, BNSS/BSA era) - TRANSLATED FROM HINDI

details.text: Kit software and interfaces: Incident Response Toolkit software; converters/adapters SATA to USB, IDE to USB, SCSI to USB, NVMe to USB and PCIe to USB; write blockers for USB, SATA, IDE and SCSI; boot software (to start the computer so the existing hard disk can be imaged and analysed without tampering); forensic imaging software; volatile-data collection software such as Win32DD, Win64DD, FTK Imager and Crypt Hunter.

steps.title: Isolate and triage digital devices by power state
steps.text: On reaching a scene with digital devices, keep people away from the digital evidence, equipment and power supply, then check whether the system is switched ON. If it is ON and the advice of an expert is available, follow that advice (for imaging volatile and non-volatile data) and then proceed to labelling and photography/videography. If it is ON and no expert advice is available: do not touch the keyboard, do not take advice from the owner, make a note of what is on the screen and photograph it, allow the printer to complete the printing, and remove the power cables from the suspected system. If the system is not switched ON, verify the power state and proceed to labelling and photography/videography.
steps.responsible: First responder / Investigating Officer at the digital scene
steps.applies_when: Digital devices are found at the scene
steps.triage_why: Improper handling of a powered-on device can lead to the loss of volatile data (RAM) or trigger remote wipes, destroying critical evidence.

ticks.do: Keep people away from the digital evidence, the equipment and the power supply on reaching a scene with digital devices.
Check whether the system is switched ON.
Follow the expert's advice for imaging volatile and non-volatile data where the system is ON and the advice of an expert is available, then proceed to labelling and photography/videography.
Take each of the following steps where the system is ON and no expert advice is available.
sub: Do not touch the keyboard.
Do not take advice from the owner.

Allow the printer to complete the printing.
Remove the power cables from the suspected system.

ticks.do: Verify the power state and proceed to labelling and photography/videography where the system is not switched ON.

details.text: If the system is switched on, record everything open and visible on the screen — all graphics and files displayed can be entered as electronic evidence; this evidence can only be recorded through video and photograph and entered by means of a written description.

steps.title: Label, Record and Remove the Seized Equipment
steps.text: Label and photograph or videograph the equipment, remove all connection cables, document/record all details and remove the equipment, ensuring that all the components have proper exhibit labels attached; then submit all the evidence for forensic examination.
steps.applies_when: Digital devices are being seized
steps.triage_why: Documentation and labeling are essential for the chain of custody. Without this, the evidence can be challenged as tampered with or planted.

Remove all connection cables.
Document and record all details.
Remove the equipment, ensuring that all the components have proper exhibit labels attached.
Submit all the evidence for forensic examination.

details.text: Documentation of the scene is a very important stage of the investigation: record the physical condition of the computer, the related equipment and the other evidence exactly as found; photography/videography is the best source for sketching and reconstructing the scene of crime.

steps.title: Mention the Chain of Custody in the Case Diary
steps.text: Mention in the case diary the chain of custody (date, time, place, etc.) of all documents, including seized electronic devices, so that it may be duly proved in Court during the trial.
steps.triage_why: A break in the chain of custody for electronic devices is a primary ground for the court to reject evidence under the BSA/Evidence Act.

steps.title: Forward the Seizure List and Property to Court
steps.text: Send the original seizure list to the Court as soon as possible, and forward the seized property and documents to the Court in the prescribed forwarding forms — with the execution report where the search was on a warrant, or with a report where it was without warrant. For obtaining expert opinion on a seized article, forward the article through the Court.
steps.deadline: Original seizure list to the Court as soon as possible (state SOP para 18(i))
steps.triage_why: Statutory requirement for the legal transfer of seized property to the court; failure to do so violates criminal procedure and jeopardizes the trial.

steps.title: Apply BNSS 103 to Closed-Place Searches
steps.text: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search [BNSS 103]: Whenever any place liable to search or inspection under Chapter VII is closed, any person residing in or being in charge of such place SHALL, on demand of the officer or other person executing the warrant and on production of the warrant, allow him free ingress thereto and afford all reasonable facilities for a search therein; if ingress cannot be so obtained, the executing officer or other person MAY proceed in the manner provided by sub-section (2) of section 44. Where any person in or about such place is reasonably suspected of concealing about his person any article for which search should be made, such person MAY be searched, and if such person is a woman the search SHALL be made by another woman with strict regard to decency. Before making a search under this Chapter the officer or other person about to make it SHALL call upon two or more independent and respectable inhabitants of the locality in which the place to be searched is situate, or of any other locality if no such inhabitant of the said locality is available or is willing to be a witness to the search, to attend and witness the search, and MAY issue an order in writing to them or any of them so to do. The search SHALL be made in their presence, and a list of all things seized in the course of such search and of the places in which they are respectively found SHALL be prepared by such officer or other person and signed by such witnesses, but no person witnessing a search under this section shall be required to attend the Court as a witness of the search unless specially summoned by it. The occupant of the place searched, or some person in his behalf, SHALL in every instance be permitted to attend during the search, and a copy of the list prepared under this section, signed by the said witnesses, SHALL be delivered to such occupant or person.
steps.stage: Statutory basis of search and seizure
legal_basis: Section 103 BNSS 2023
steps.deadline: Section 105 (applies to the section 103 search and seizure-list process): the police officer shall 'without delay' forward the audio-video recording to the District Magistrate, Sub-divisional Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class
steps.triage_why: Describes a statutory power/duty of a person in charge of a premises; it is a rule of law to be applied if the situation arises.

steps.title: Seize and Report Property Under BNSS 106
steps.text: Power of police officer to seize certain property [BNSS 106]: Any police officer MAY seize any property which may be alleged or suspected to have been stolen, or which may be found under circumstances which create suspicion of the commission of any offence - the seizure power is permissive and belongs to any police officer. The reporting duties that follow are mandatory: such police officer, if subordinate to the officer in charge of a police station, SHALL forthwith report the seizure to that officer, and every police officer acting under sub-section (1) SHALL forthwith report the seizure to the Magistrate having jurisdiction. Within the same sub-section (3), where the property seized cannot be conveniently transported to the Court, or where there is difficulty in securing proper accommodation for its custody, or where continued retention of the property in police custody may not be considered necessary for the purpose of investigation, he MAY give custody thereof to any person on his executing a bond undertaking to produce the property before the Court as and when required and to give effect to the further orders of the Court as to the disposal of the same. By the proviso, where property seized under sub-section (1) is subject to speedy and natural decay and the person entitled to possession is unknown or absent and the value of such property is less than five hundred rupees, it MAY forthwith be sold by auction under the orders of the Superintendent of Police, and the provisions of sections 503 and 504 shall, as nearly as may be practicable, apply to the net proceeds of such sale.
steps.stage: Statutory basis of search and seizure
legal_basis: Section 106 BNSS 2023
steps.deadline: 'Forthwith' - a subordinate police officer's report of the seizure to the officer in charge of the police station (sub-section (2)); 'Forthwith' - every police officer acting under sub-section (1) must report the seizure to the Magistrate having jurisdiction (sub-section (3)); 'Forthwith' - the permissive auction sale of perishable property meeting the proviso conditions, under the orders of the Superintendent of Police
steps.triage_why: Defines the legal power of seizure under BNSS; it is a background legal authority.

steps.title: Route Out-of-Station Searches Through BNSS 186
steps.text: When officer in charge of police station may require another to issue search-warrant [BNSS 186]: Sub-section (1) is permissive: an officer in charge of a police station or a police officer not being below the rank of sub-inspector making an investigation "may require" an officer in charge of another police station, whether in the same or a different district, to cause a search to be made in any place, in any case in which the former officer might cause such search to be made, within the limits of his own station. Sub-section (2) is mandatory on the officer who receives the requisition: such officer, on being so required, shall proceed according to the provisions of section 185, and shall forward the thing found, if any, to the officer at whose request the search was made. Sub-section (3) supplies an urgency route in enabling terms - whenever there is reason to believe that the delay occasioned by requiring an officer in charge of another police station to cause a search to be made under sub-section (1) might result in evidence of the commission of an offence being concealed or destroyed, "it shall be lawful for" an officer in charge of a police station or a police officer making any investigation under this Chapter to search, or cause to be searched, any place in the limits of another police station in accordance with the provisions of section 185, as if such place were within the limits of his own police station; this confers lawful authority, it does not compel a search. Sub-section (4) then imposes mandatory post-search intimation: any officer conducting a search under sub-section (3) shall forthwith send notice of the search to the officer in charge of the police station within the limits of which such place is situate, shall also send with such notice a copy of the list (if any) prepared under section 103, and shall also send to the nearest Magistrate empowered to take cognizance of the offence copies of the records referred to in sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 185. Sub-section (5) requires that the owner or occupier of the place searched shall, on application, be furnished free of cost with a copy of any record sent to the Magistrate under sub-section (4).
steps.stage: Statutory basis of search and seizure
legal_basis: Section 186 BNSS 2023
steps.deadline: Sub-section (4): notice of a search conducted under sub-section (3) shall be sent "forthwith" to the officer in charge of the police station within the limits of which the searched place is situate. No fixed number of hours is printed anywhere in section 186. (Do not import the "forthwith, but not later than forty-eight hours" figure printed on the same PDF page 73 - that period belongs to section 185(5), which governs copies of records made under section 185(1) or 185(3).)
steps.triage_why: Describes a procedural option for inter-station cooperation; only needed if the search is outside the registering station's jurisdiction.

ticks.do: Require an officer in charge of another police station, whether in the same or a different district, to cause a search to be made in any place.
notes: Permissive - sub-section (1) says the officer 'may require'.

Available to an officer in charge of a police station or a police officer not below the rank of sub-inspector making an investigation, in any case in which he might cause such search within the limits of his own station.

ticks.do: Proceed according to the provisions of section 185 on being so required, and forward the thing found, if any, to the officer at whose request the search was made.
notes: Mandatory on the officer who receives the requisition.

ticks.do: Search, or cause to be searched, any place in the limits of another police station in accordance with the provisions of section 185, as if it were within the limits of your own police station.
notes: Available whenever there is reason to believe that the delay occasioned by requiring an officer in charge of another police station to cause a search under sub-section (1) might result in evidence of the commission of an offence being concealed or destroyed.
Sub-section (3) says 'it shall be lawful for' the officer to do so; it confers lawful authority, it does not compel a search.

ticks.do: Send notice of a search conducted under sub-section (3) forthwith to the officer in charge of the police station within the limits of which such place is situate.
notes: Mandatory.

No fixed number of hours is printed anywhere in section 186; the 'forthwith, but not later than forty-eight hours' period belongs to section 185(5), which governs copies of records made under section 185(1) or 185(3).

ticks.do: Send with such notice a copy of the list (if any) prepared under section 103.
Send to the nearest Magistrate empowered to take cognizance of the offence copies of the records referred to in sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 185.
Furnish the owner or occupier of the place searched, on application, free of cost with a copy of any record sent to the Magistrate under sub-section (4).

details.text: RANK THRESHOLD, verbatim: the requisitioning officer must be "An officer in charge of a police station or a police officer not being below the rank of sub-inspector making an investigation".
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

details.text: PERMISSIVE: such an officer MAY require an officer in charge of another police station - whether in the same or a different district - to cause a search to be made in any place.
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

details.text: Scope limit on the requisition: it extends only to "any case in which the former officer might cause such search to be made, within the limits of his own station".
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

details.text: MANDATORY on the requested officer: such officer, on being so required, SHALL proceed according to the provisions of section 185, and shall forward the thing found, if any, to the officer at whose request the search was made.
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

details.text: Urgency trigger for sub-section (3), verbatim scope: reason to believe that the delay occasioned by requiring an officer in charge of another police station to cause a search to be made UNDER SUB-SECTION (1) might result in evidence of the commission of an offence being concealed or destroyed.
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

details.text: ENABLING LANGUAGE in sub-section (3): "it shall be lawful for an officer in charge of a police station or a police officer making any investigation under this Chapter to search, or cause to be searched, any place in the limits of another police station in accordance with the provisions of section 185, as if such place were within the limits of his own police station". This authorises; it does not direct or require a search.
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

details.text: After a sub-section (3) search, the officer SHALL FORTHWITH send notice of the search to the officer in charge of the police station within the limits of which such place is situate.
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

details.text: He shall also send with such notice a copy of the list (if any) prepared under section 103.
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

details.text: He shall also send to the nearest Magistrate empowered to take cognizance of the offence copies of the records referred to in sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 185.
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

details.text: Sub-section (5): the owner or occupier of the place searched shall, on application, be furnished FREE OF COST with a copy of any record sent to the Magistrate under sub-section (4).
details.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

steps.title: Record necessity grounds for arrest in seven-year cases
steps.text: For cognizable offences punishable with 7 years or less, arrest only if satisfied one necessity condition exists and record the reasons in writing at the time of arrest: (1) to prevent further offence; (2) for proper investigation; (3) to prevent disappearance/tampering of evidence; (4) to prevent inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts to dissuade disclosure to the Court or police; (5) the person's presence in Court cannot otherwise be ensured. In every case where arrest is not necessary, equally record in writing the reasons for not arresting.
legal_basis: BNSS 35(1)(b)(ii)
BNSS 35(1)(b) proviso
steps.applies_when: Cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years
steps.triage_why: Statutory mandate for arrests in offences punishable by 7 years or less; failure to record reasons in writing makes the arrest illegal.

ticks.do: Arrest for a cognizable offence punishable with 7 years or less only if satisfied that one necessity condition exists [BNSS 35(1)(b)(ii)]:
sub: (1) To prevent further offence.
(2) For proper investigation.
(3) To prevent disappearance or tampering of evidence.
(4) To prevent inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts to dissuade disclosure to the Court or police.
(5) The person's presence in Court cannot otherwise be ensured.

ticks.do: Record the reasons in writing at the time of arrest.
Record in writing the reasons for not arresting in every case where arrest is not necessary [BNSS 35(1)(b) proviso].

details.text: Submit the recorded reasons together with the checklist as per Appendix-1 of the Gujarat SOP.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: The Annexure-1 checklist records the police station, case number/sections, arresting officer, accused particulars, offence and maximum punishment, whether the s.35(3) notice was given and whether the accused appeared in reference to it, and the satisfying ground — the five statutory grounds plus a sixth: failure to comply with the terms of the notice or unwillingness to give his own identity — with brief facts/evidence and the arresting officer's signature.

details.text: Record the reason for not arresting in the Case Diary; written reasons are not required for offences punishable with more than 7 years.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Before arresting, evaluate the evidence available and the necessity of arrest (whether the person will be put under trial, is likely to tamper with or destroy evidence, or escape the process of law) and avoid unnecessary publicity of the arrest.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Once the suspect has been identified and the evidence is sufficient, make the arrest. Follow proper procedures during the arrest and ensure that the suspect's rights are protected.

steps.title: Arrest only under a law authorising arrest
steps.text: Make no arrest except in accordance with the BNSS or another law in force authorising arrest — an arrest outside these provisions is illegal.
legal_basis: BNSS 62
steps.triage_why: Fundamental statutory duty; an illegal arrest can lead to the quashing of proceedings or civil liability for the officer.

ticks.do: Make no arrest except in accordance with the BNSS or another law in force authorising arrest.
notes: An arrest outside these provisions is illegal.

details.text: An IO who fails to comply with the BNSS arrest provisions is liable to departmental disciplinary action under the rules in force.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Where a special Act applies (e.g. the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act), strictly follow its additional provisions.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Exercise the power of arrest without warrant with utmost care; it takes away individual liberty and human rights must not be violated.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

details.text: Before making any arrest, consider whether there are proper grounds for the arrest and whether the arrest is necessary; no person is to be arrested merely because the police possess the power to arrest, and no arbitrary arrest may be made without following due process.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Do not arrest just because it is lawful to do so; the police officer must be able to justify the arrest apart from the power to make it.
details.citation: Kerala Police - Standard Operating Procedure: Investigation & Prosecution in General (SOP Series), State Police Chief, 01.11.2020

steps.title: Verify the ground for a warrantless arrest
steps.text: Before a warrantless arrest, verify the person falls in a BNSS 35(1) category: (i) commits a cognizable offence in police presence; (ii) credible information received that he has committed a cognizable offence punishable with more than 7 years or death, with reason to believe on the basis of that information that he committed it; (iii) credible information or reasonable suspicion of a cognizable offence punishable up to 7 years, with a recorded necessity ground; (iv) proclaimed offender; (v) possession of suspected stolen property with reasonable suspicion of an offence; (vi) obstructing police in duty or escaping/attempting escape from lawful custody; (vii) armed-forces deserter; (viii) extraditable act committed abroad; (ix) released convict breaching the release-condition rules under s.394(5); (x) requisition (written or oral, specifying the person and the offence or other cause) from another police officer who could lawfully arrest that person without warrant. In a non-cognizable case do not arrest except under a warrant or Magistrate's order (subject to s.39).
legal_basis: BNSS 35(1)
BNSS 35(2)
steps.triage_why: Statutory prerequisite for warrantless arrest; failure to verify these categories renders the arrest unlawful.

ticks.do: Verify before a warrantless arrest that the person falls in one of the BNSS 35(1) categories:
sub: (i) Commits a cognizable offence in police presence.
(ii) Credible information received that he has committed a cognizable offence punishable with more than 7 years or death, with reason to believe on the basis of that information that he committed it.
(iii) Credible information or reasonable suspicion of a cognizable offence punishable up to 7 years, with a recorded necessity ground.
(iv) Proclaimed offender.
(v) Possession of suspected stolen property with reasonable suspicion of an offence.
(vi) Obstructing police in duty or escaping or attempting escape from lawful custody.
(vii) Armed-forces deserter.
(viii) Extraditable act committed abroad.
(ix) Released convict breaching the release-condition rules under s.394(5).
(x) Requisition (written or oral, specifying the person and the offence or other cause) from another police officer who could lawfully arrest that person without warrant.

ticks.do: Do not arrest in a non-cognizable case except under a warrant or a Magistrate's order [BNSS 35(2)].
notes: Subject to s.39.

steps.title: Obtain DySP permission before arresting the infirm or elderly
steps.text: Do not arrest a person who is infirm or above 60 years of age for an offence punishable with less than 3 years' imprisonment without the prior permission of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.
legal_basis: BNSS 35(7)
steps.applies_when: Offence punishable with less than 3 years and arrestee infirm or above 60 years
steps.triage_why: A specific rule that applies only if the accused is infirm or over 60; not applicable to the general case unless the accused meets these criteria.

ticks.do: Check whether the person is infirm or above 60 years of age and whether the offence is punishable with less than 3 years' imprisonment [BNSS 35(7)].
Obtain the prior permission of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police before arresting such a person.

details.text: Obtain the permission from the DySP/SDPO/ACP of the officer's jurisdiction or any superior police officer, and obtain documents relating to the infirmity and age of the person.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

steps.title: Issue a notice of appearance instead of arresting
steps.text: In all cognizable cases where arrest is not necessary, issue the person a notice of appearance under BNSS 35(3) directing him to appear before the officer at a stated date, time and place. A person who complies (and continues to comply) with the notice shall not be arrested for that offence unless the officer records specific reasons; on failure to comply or refusal to identify himself, the officer may arrest him (BNSS 35(6)), subject to any Court orders.
legal_basis: BNSS 35(3)
BNSS 35(5)
BNSS 35(6)
steps.triage_why: Standard procedure for non-necessary arrests, but not a statutory duty that defeats the case if a direct arrest is instead justified by the gravity of POCSO/BNS charges.

ticks.do: Issue the person a notice of appearance under BNSS 35(3) directing him to appear before the officer at a stated date, time and place, in all cognizable cases where arrest is not necessary.
Do not arrest for that offence a person who complies, and continues to comply, with the notice, unless the officer records specific reasons [BNSS 35(5)].
Arrest him on failure to comply with the notice or on refusal to identify himself [BNSS 35(6)].
notes: The officer may so arrest, subject to any Court orders.

details.text: Use the notice specimen at Appendix-2; the IO may impose necessary terms and conditions in the notice (specimen at Appendix-2A), the recipient must comply with them, and if he does not comply the IO may arrest him.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Appendix-2 is the Notice for Appearance before the Police (Second Schedule Form No. 1, see Section 522 / Section 35(3) BNSS), directing the accused/suspect to appear before the officer at a stated date, time and place for questioning.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: The Appendix-2A terms and conditions (Sections 35(3) and 35(6) BNSS) require appearance before the Court/IO, truthful disclosure, production of documents/material, no destruction of evidence, and no threat/inducement/promise to persons acquainted with the facts.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Obtain a written acknowledgement of receipt of the notice from the person served (Appendix-2B); when he appears pursuant to the notice and demands a written receipt of his appearance, give a receipt as per Annexure-2C.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Annexure-2B is a signed acknowledgement of having received the notice, with an undertaking to co-operate; non-compliance attracts legal liability.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Annexure-2C records the notice-recipient's attendance (date and hours), the entry in the police-station register, the seizure/production memo of any documents produced, and an assurance of compliance with future notices; it is signed by the accused, an independent witness and the IO.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: If the person communicates written reasons within a reasonable time explaining inability to appear on the notified date/time, a fresh date may be granted only where the officer has reason to believe there are sufficient and proper grounds, and a note of such reasons shall be made in the case diary; the request shall not be accepted if time is being sought to evade or delay the investigation.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Mention in the case diary the action taken in respect of the notice.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: Maintain at the police station a register (specimen at Appendix-3) of accused/suspect persons to whom notices under Section 35(3) BNSS have been given.
details.citation: Twenty-Nine Standard Operating Procedures - C.I.D. Crime & Railways, Gujarat Police, circular PRC/Circular-SOP-1/656/2024 dated 29/10/2024

details.text: The Appendix-3 register records the case reference, the noticee's name/address/mobile/e-mail/Aadhaar, the date, time and place of appearance and departure, and the signatures of the accused/suspect, the IO and the Station House Officer.

steps.title: Check for interim protection before arresting
steps.text: Do not arrest where a Court has granted interim protection or a stay. If the accused declares anticipatory bail has been granted but the IO has received no order, verify the matter and then take further necessary action.
steps.triage_why: Arresting a person protected by a court stay is a violation of judicial orders and can lead to contempt of court and immediate release of the accused.

ticks.do: Do not arrest where a Court has granted interim protection or a stay.
Verify the matter and then take further necessary action where the accused declares anticipatory bail has been granted but the IO has received no order.

steps.title: Take over a person arrested by a private person
steps.text: A private person may arrest someone who commits a non-bailable and cognizable offence in his presence, or any proclaimed offender, and must hand the person over to a police officer or take him to the nearest police station without unnecessary delay and within six hours. The police officer must take the person into custody (re-arrest) if BNSS 35(1) applies; if the person appears to have committed a non-cognizable offence and refuses his name/residence or gives false particulars, deal with him under s.39; if there is no sufficient ground to believe any offence was committed, release him at once.
steps.stage: Arrest powers of others & warrant execution
legal_basis: BNSS 40
steps.deadline: Handover to police within 6 hours of the private arrest, and without unnecessary delay
steps.triage_why: Describes the power of a private person to arrest; it is not a duty of the Investigating Officer.

ticks.do: Recognise that a private person may arrest someone who commits a non-bailable and cognizable offence in his presence, or any proclaimed offender [BNSS 40].
Require the private person to hand the arrested person over to a police officer, or take him to the nearest police station, without unnecessary delay and within six hours.
Take the person into custody, re-arresting him, if BNSS 35(1) applies.
notes: The police officer must do so.

ticks.do: Deal with him under s.39 if he appears to have committed a non-cognizable offence and refuses his name or residence or gives false particulars.
Release him at once if there is no sufficient ground to believe any offence was committed.

steps.title: Inform designated officers of a warrant arrest
steps.text: On arrest of any person on the basis of a warrant, immediately give information of the arrest and of the place where the arrested person is kept to the designated police officer of the district and to such officer of the other district where the arrested person ordinarily resides (Section 82(2) BNSS).
steps.stage: Arrest powers of others & warrant execution
legal_basis: BNSS 82(2)
steps.deadline: Immediately on arrest
steps.triage_why: Statutory requirement under BNSS 82(2) to inform designated officers; failure is a procedural lapse in custodial transparency.

ticks.do: Give information of the arrest and of the place where the arrested person is kept immediately on arrest of any person on the basis of a warrant (Section 82(2) BNSS), to each of the following:
sub: The designated police officer of the district.
The designated officer of the other district where the arrested person ordinarily resides.

steps.title: Exercise the Magistrate's power to arrest offenders
steps.text: Any Magistrate, Executive or Judicial, may himself arrest or order any person to arrest an offender who commits an offence in his presence within his local jurisdiction, and may then commit the offender to custody subject to the bail provisions; a Magistrate may also at any time arrest, or direct the arrest in his presence within his local jurisdiction, of any person for whose arrest he is at that time competent to issue a warrant.
steps.stage: Arrest powers of others & warrant execution
legal_basis: BNSS 41
steps.triage_why: Describes the powers of a Magistrate to arrest; not a duty of the IO.

ticks.do: Arrest, or order any person to arrest, an offender who commits an offence in the Magistrate's presence within his local jurisdiction [BNSS 41].
notes: Any Magistrate, Executive or Judicial, may do this.

ticks.do: Commit the offender to custody thereafter, subject to the bail provisions.
notes: The Magistrate may then so commit him.

ticks.do: Arrest, or direct the arrest in his presence within his local jurisdiction, of any person for whose arrest the Magistrate is at that time competent to issue a warrant.
notes: A Magistrate may do this at any time.

sources.citation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
sources.authority: law (statute)

steps.title: Depute a subordinate to arrest by written order
steps.text: When the officer in charge of a police station or an investigating officer requires a subordinate to arrest a person without warrant (otherwise than in his presence), deliver to the subordinate a written order specifying the person to be arrested and the offence or other cause of arrest. Before making the arrest, the deputed officer must notify the substance of the order to the person and show him the order if he so requires. This does not affect the officer's own power of arrest under s.35.
steps.stage: Arrest powers of others & warrant execution
legal_basis: BNSS 55(1)
steps.triage_why: Statutory requirement for written orders when delegating arrest to subordinates to ensure legality of the custody.

ticks.do: Deliver to the subordinate a written order specifying the person to be arrested and the offence or other cause of arrest [BNSS 55(1)].
notes: Applies when the officer in charge of a police station or an investigating officer requires a subordinate to arrest a person without warrant, otherwise than in his presence.
This does not affect the officer's own power of arrest under s.35.

steps.title: Execute the endorsed arrest warrant and produce the arrestee
steps.text: Execute an arrest warrant endorsed to the officer for execution — there is no discretion in executing the warrant. If the arrest cannot be made within the time specified in the warrant, return the unexecuted warrant and obtain a fresh warrant. When the arrest is made within the issuing Court's jurisdiction, produce the arrestee before that Court at the earliest and in any case within 24 hours.
steps.stage: Arrest powers of others & warrant execution
steps.deadline: Production before the issuing Court at the earliest, in any case within 24 hours
steps.triage_why: Executing a warrant is a mandatory judicial order; failure to produce the arrestee within 24 hours is a violation of constitutional rights.

steps.title: Execute a warrant beyond the issuing Court's jurisdiction
steps.text: To execute a warrant directed to a police officer beyond the local jurisdiction of the issuing Court, ordinarily take it for endorsement either to an Executive Magistrate or to a police officer not below the rank of officer-in-charge of a police station within whose local limits it is to be executed; the local police shall, if required, assist in executing it (s.79 CrPC [now BNSS 81]). Where the warrant is executed outside the issuing district and the issuing Court is beyond 30 km from the place of execution, produce the arrestee before the Executive Magistrate, District Superintendent of Police or Commissioner of Police in whose jurisdiction the warrant was executed (s.80 CrPC [now BNSS 82]) and obtain that authority's orders for production before the issuing Court.
steps.stage: Arrest powers of others & warrant execution
legal_basis: Section 79 CrPC [now BNSS 81]
Section 80 CrPC [now BNSS 82]
steps.triage_why: Necessary legal procedure for executing warrants outside local jurisdiction to ensure the arrest is lawful.

ticks.do: Take the warrant ordinarily for endorsement to one of the following, within whose local limits it is to be executed (s.79 CrPC [now BNSS 81]):

A police officer not below the rank of officer-in-charge of a police station.
notes: The local police shall, if required, assist in executing it.

ticks.do: Produce the arrestee before the Executive Magistrate, District Superintendent of Police or Commissioner of Police in whose jurisdiction the warrant was executed (s.80 CrPC [now BNSS 82]).

ticks.do: Obtain that authority's orders for production before the issuing Court.

steps.title: Wear identification and prepare the arrest memorandum
steps.text: Every officer making an arrest shall: bear an accurate, visible and clear identification of his name; prepare a memorandum of arrest attested by at least one witness who is a family member of the arrestee or a respectable member of the locality of arrest and countersigned by the arrested person; and, unless the memo is attested by a family member, inform the arrestee of his right to have a relative, friend or nominated person informed of the arrest (BNSS 36 / D.K. Basu directives).
legal_basis: BNSS 36
steps.triage_why: The arrest memorandum is a mandatory statutory document; its absence is a major procedural flaw that can jeopardize the prosecution.

sub: A family member of the arrestee.
A respectable member of the locality of the arrest.
